News.title: New ‘status’ dogs dubbed ‘XL Bullies on steroids’ loved by celebs & criminals on sale for £75 after boy mauled to death
News.content:
A SIMPLE walk to the shops turned into a nightmare for mum Abbie Craig, earlier this month, when she was wrenched to the ground and rendered helpless as a powerful dog ripped chunks from her flesh – so much so, she now faces losing her arm.

But the dog wasn’t the outlawed XL Bully so demonised in recent years, but a rising new breed on the block, the current “status dog” – which is on sale for £75 and described as a Bully “on steroids” with a bite “stronger than a lion”.





The Cane Corso – a mastiff type – can grow up to 50kg and has been linked to a growing list of gruesome attacks across the UK, including the fatal mauling of three-year-old Daniel Twigg.

Tory MP Gregory Stafford has formally asked the government to “make an assessment of the potential merits” of adding the unofficial breed to the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991’s banned list.

Celebrity owners of the Corso include footballer Marcus Rashford, Hollywood star Vin Diesel, Love Island contestant Jack Fincham, and Boyzone frontman Ronan Keating.

But canine behaviour specialist and founder of the Canine Instructor Academy, Rob Alleyne described the breed – which a Sun investigation found was historically bred to be war dogs in countries like Romania – as far worse than XL Bullies, labelling them a “killing machine”.

Website Pets4Homes currently lists 129 such dogs for sale in the UK – with three of the animals priced at as little as £75.

Mr Alleyne told us: “It’s a killing machine and they’ve become much more popular now.”





He added the Bully ban has “pushed people towards an even worse dog that doesn’t need to be registered and God help us if they become too popular”.

Veterinary nurse and dog trainer Wendy Cummins agrees Corsos – not recognised as an official breed by the UK Kennel Club – appear to be replacing the XL Bully since it was outlawed in February 2024, to dangerous effect.

Wendy told the Sun this week “in the hands of idiots they’re just dangerous”, adding: “It’s a massive status symbol.”

Her surgery has had to euthanise a number of Corsos due to uncontrollable aggression – and she says dog shelters are full of them as ignorant owners realise they’re simply too much to handle.

And while some older dogs are selling cheaply, many breeders are cashing in on the popularity of the breed. One litter of nine puppies at just a week old, currently listed in Bedworth, Warwickshire, for £3,000 each, are described as having a “Romanian bloodline”.

Another seller, in Aldershot, Hampshire, is offering five eight-week-old Corso puppies at £4,000 – boasting: “We are delighted to offer an exceptional litter of Cane Corso puppies from carefully selected European Champion bloodlines”.



Mum-of-two Abbie Craig told us in tears from her hospital bed earlier this month how she feared she would die as she was rag-dolled in the street and chunks of flesh were torn off during the random attack in Crawley, Sussex, on July 11 – with the Corso owner subsequently arrested.

A Good Samaritan neighbour called Danny stepped in to help and was also mauled, before being taken to hospital with horror injuries.

The incident sparked a fresh debate into the effectiveness of the banned dogs list, which includes, alongside the XL Bully, the Pit Bull Terrior, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino and Fila Brasileiro.

Corsos have been behind at least two fatal attacks in the UK, including that of three-year-old Daniel Twigg, who, unsupervised for a mere 15 minutes, had crept into a breeding dog pen at a farm in Rochdale, South Yorkshire, in May 2022.

He was killed by two Corsos – named Sid and Tiny – in a horror attack, with his parents Mark Twigg and Joanne Bedford found guilty in October last year of being in charge of a dangerous dog which caused injury, and jailed.

Months later in April 2023, 51-year-old Wayne Stevens was also mauled to death in Derby by his brother Gary Stevens’ Cane Corso cross – with the owner also jailed.

The previous January, a Cane Corso attacked an unnamed 16-year-old girl in Doncaster, South Yorkshire, requiring her to undergo extensive reconstructive surgery.

While Charlotte Potts, 32, was subjected to a similar horror attack on July 4 this year when her own Cane Corso – which she had adopted just weeks before – turned on her while she was playing fetch with it.



Some police forces have noted a shift in criminal ownership, with gang members and irresponsible owners actively replacing seized XL Bullies with Corsos and other large protection breeds – including, reportedly, for intimidation and protection work.

FOI results from forces including Essex and Kent, also show Corsos are steadily climbing the ranks of non-banned breeds being seized under Section 3 of the Dangerous Dogs Act.

UK-based campaign group Protect Our Pets has actively lobbied the government to expand the Act, arguing the Corso possesses an aggressive “fighting heritage” – urging immediate, pre-emptive steps to restrict the breed before the problem escalates further.

And Peta UK is also campaigning against the continued breeding of large, powerful mastiff and bully-type dogs.

The organisation has called for a mandatory spay and neuter ban on Corsos to phase the breed out – arguing they are inherently high-risk in typical residential settings.

However, vet and trainer Wendy is among a raft of experts who, while accepting the breed is dangerous in the wrong hands, is not solely to blame and should not be banned.

Referring to people buying Corsos for status, she told The Sun “it’s not what they’re for, it’s absolutely heart-breaking”.

Wendy explained: “The Cane Corso is a beautiful Italian mastiff.



“It’s a fantastic sports dog but in the hands of idiots they’re just dangerous.

“They’re really trainable, there’s no excuse for them being out of control.

“But they’re being handled by ignorant people.”

She added that the breed tend to be favoured by a “particular type of person” who don’t socialise them properly, making them a threat to the public.

And like Bullies, Wendy said Corsos are often subjected to the cruel act of cropping ears – a practice illegal in the UK – “which can make them look more menacing”.

The trainer went on to say: “These owners’ intentions are clearly bad from the start.”

Dr Aimee Warner, resident veterinarian at pet insurance company Waggel, said: “Aggression in dogs is complex.

“Genetics may play a part, but breeding, early experiences, socialisation, training, physical health, fear, pain, the home environment and handling can all influence behaviour.”

She added that owners should focus on responsible breeding and ownership, early socialisation and reward-based training to minimise aggressive behaviour.

Personal injury lawyer Benson Varghese notes that reducing the number of attacks is about shifting the focus from breed to behaviour.



“If people who want to have a powerful “status” dog will just move from the unlawful to some other lawful, still aggressive breeds, then legislation would be reactive, rather than proactive,” he said.

“Therefore, the discussion about the Cane Corso being prohibited or not should go further than the ban or prohibition of this breed. It should include discussion about ownership, breeding, training, and liability.”

Over 9,000 people are hospitalised annually in the UK because of dog bites or attacks, highlighting the importance of taking “urgent action” on the matter, he added.

RSPCA Dog Welfare Expert and Dog Control Lead, Dr Samantha Gaines, said the charity are urging the government to tackle irresponsible breeding and enforce stricter legislation against illegal practices.

“We have also been actively calling for accurate and detailed recording and monitoring of dangerous dog incidents as this will help us understand the scale of dog bites and what causes them,” she said.

A spokesperson for DEFRA said: “Owners of any breed of dog which is dangerously out of control are breaking the law.

“We are working to explore measures to reduce dog attacks and promote responsible dog ownership across all breeds of dog.

“We continue to work with the police, local authorities and animal welfare groups to prevent dog attacks by addressing dog control issues before they escalate and using the full force of the law where needed.”

News.title: Europe’s migrant weak spots from Channel to tiny enclaves and vast TUNNELS – as THOUSANDS storm Spanish beach
News.content:
EUROPE is facing a multi-pronged surge in migrants smashing through key weak spots in the continent’s border defences.

Violence erupted this week as hundreds more migrants crossed the English Channel into the UK as up to 60,000 stormed the beaches of a Spanish enclave sparking an army mobilisation.



Streams of illegal migrants are also coming from Turkey, Libya and Western Africa into Brit holiday hotspots in Greece, Cyprus and the Canary Islands.

The Italians are also experiencing an uptick in migration figures as PM Giorgia Meloni said this week “uncontrolled illegal immigration poses a concrete threat to the security of Europe’s borders”.



There are currently five main routes being abused by migrants and traffickers as they battle to make it into Europe and remain there illegally.

The one which is hitting hardest due to being closest to home is the English Channel route.

A flotilla of up to 1,000 migrants headed for Britain overnight as French cops watched on with instructions “to let them go”.

A worrying total of 752 migrants reached the UK on Wednesday in the biggest day of Channel crossings this year.



Four migrants also died trying to cross the Channel with three found dead aboard a boat off Dunkirk while a fourth is believed to have drowned in a separate incident near Boulogne-sur-Mer.

The Channel has been a major weak spot for years now as debates continue to rage on over whether the migrant issue is a French or English problem.



New PM Andy Burnham has insisted Labour’s plan to clamp down on illegal migration was working.

Despite being down 45 per cent on 2025, more than 13,007 migrants have still crossed the Channel this year.

Part of Labour’s plan saw them hand the French over £1billion from UK taxpayers to stop migrants crossing.

Under the deal, the UK said it will withhold cash if the French police are failing to deliver value for money.



But French cops who watch on openly admit they are still told to let them cross as it is “too dangerous” to stop them.

Tony Smith, the ex-Director General of the UK Border Force, previously told The Sun that migrants are taking advantage of legal loopholes once they’re in British territory.

He said: “Asylum effectively trumps border control. Once they’ve mentioned the magic word they’re in.

“All they’ve got to say is they’re in fear of persecution or I’m worried about their human rights from wherever I’m from, you can’t send me back.



“Our hands are tied.

“Unless we get some significant change over what we’ve been getting over the last seven years this will continue – it needs something drastic.”

Similar issues are flaring up for the Spanish with migrants constantly making the daring journey from Africa across to European territory.

Spain mobilised its army after an estimated 60,000 migrants stormed a border crossing in just 24 hours.



Footage captured migrants flooding into Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in northern Africa, from Morocco and causing havoc.

At least 67 people died during the swim and resulting stampede as tanks and soldiers were deployed on the streets as they shut down the border.

Hundreds also made it to Melilla, a second Spanish enclave, where shots were fired at the border as people broke through fences.

Ceuta and Melilla have become plagued by weak spots in recent years as migrants figure out new ways to bypass the borders.



Dozens have reportedly started to attempt to crawl through drainage conduits, runoff pipes, and culverts running underneath the border walls.

This can be done during dry weather or low-water periods in the Strait of Gibraltar such as this year due to the heatwave conditions in Europe.

Often these tunnels can be created by smugglers who get paid by migrants to help them cross borders regardless of the risk to life.

The Canary Islands are also facing migration woes with 18,000 people coming over from Mauritania, Senegal and Cote d’Ivoire in 2025.



Fears are now rising that there could be an influx in the number of migrants in the coming weeks due to a “woke” Supreme Court ruling in Spain.

Migrants intercepted while swimming to the Spanish territories are now not subject to immediate expulsion per the ruling three weeks ago.

It found that entering by sea does not involve crossing a physical land border, making “hot returns” inapplicable to existing immigration laws.

The decision has been exploited by people-smuggling gangs and brought with it a wave of undocumented migration helped by Spain‘s socialist government with a pro-migration stance.



Spain and the UK’s failings to curb the migrant crisis have provoked outrage from their continental neighbours.

Italian PM Meloni said after watching the chaos in Ceuta she is prepared to ban Spain from the Schengen area completely.

The Schengen area is a passport-free travel zone made up of 29 European countries where people can move freely without internal border checks.

The UK is also not a part of the zone.



But Meloni isn’t without her own issues, with the “central migration route” seeing people entering Italy and Malta via Libya and Tunisia in their droves.

This route is known to be the deadliest in Europe with 1,342 migrants dying during the passage last year, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM).

In total, 66,000 migrants entered Italy with the majority coming from the islands of Lampedusa and Sicily, authorities believe.

Migrants have found accessible routes into Europe in almost all directions now including from the east through Turkey.



The growing migrant crisis in the UK and Europe BOTH the United Kingdom and Europe are currently battling significant challenges related to migration. The UK is grappling with a sharp rise in migration, particularly through small boat crossings across the English Channel. This has placed immense pressure on the asylum system, with thousands of asylum seekers housed in hotels, costing the government billions annually. A record number of people claimed asylum in the UK in the last year – with an estimated 32,000 living in taxpayer-funded hotels. This has prompted fury from locals who have been protesting against the housing of asylum seekers in public spaces such as hotels. Across Europe, migration policies are becoming stricter as the influence of far-right, anti-migration parties continues to grow. Spain’s holiday islands have hit breaking point with near-daily arrivals of small-boat migrants, officials say. Locals on Majorca, Ibiza, and Tenerife among others are at their “wits end” and have begun rebelling, according to island governments. Elsewhere, Italy has recently signed a controversial deal with Albania to process up to 36,000 migrants annually outside the EU. Poland, Hungary and Croatia have all also been made to bolster up their borders and strengthen ties with international allies to halt the number of migrants entering their countries. Portugal has even been forced to shut the door completely on migrants as they deploy cops on beaches and order deportations within days.

In 2025, this route was responsible for 54,666 migrants and refugees arriving in Greece, Bulgaria and Cyprus by land and sea, the IOM reports.

The migrant figures are gradually improving across Europe with IOM numbers showing 158,003 migrants arrived in Europe in the past 12 months.

This marks a 24 per cent decline from 2024 and a 46 per cent decline

compared with 2023 where the annual number was a staggering 293,000.

But experts warn this doesn’t mean the issues are close to being over.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Arnaud Banos, migration specialist at France‘s National Center for Scientific Research (CNRS), told InfoMigrants: “Departures now take place in both summer and winter.



“When governments try to stop migrants from leaving, migrants may attempt a crossing during a storm to avoid being noticed.”

News.title: Young boy and teenage girl rushed to hospital with life-changing injuries after crash between lorry & car
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

HORROR SMASH Young boy and teenage girl rushed to hospital with life-changing injuries after crash between lorry & car

A YOUNG boy and a teenage girl have been rushed to hospital with life-changing injuries after a horror crash.

Emergency services were scrambled to the A361 near Rackenford, Devon, at around 10am on Thursday.

Cops said they had been called to a serious collision involving a heavy goods vehicle with a trailer and a red MG car.

A young boy and a teenage girl sustained “suspected life-changing injuries” and were both airlifted to hospital.





A woman in her 60s was also taken to hospital with serious injuries while another woman in the car sustained minor injuries.

The driver of the lorry was discharged at the scene.

A road closure was in place while investigations took place but it has since fully re-opened.

A spokesperson for Devon and Cornwall Police said: “The Roads Policing Team would like to thank the public for their patience.



“We are appealing for any witnesses who were in the area at the time of the collision and may have seen anything or have dash camera footage.

“Police request anyone with information regarding the collision to please contact us via our website or by calling 101 quoting reference number 50260201052.”

News.title: Shocking moment Moroccan riot cops launch ROCKS at migrant as he tries to swim across into Spanish enclave
News.content:
PELTED with rocks by Moroccan riot cops, a teenage migrant plunges into the waves as he attempts to swim from Africa to European territory.

The half-hearted attempts to stop the lad were in vain.



Soon he was striking out into the Strait of Gibraltar in the wake of 60,000 others who have already reached the Spanish exclave of Ceuta since Thursday.

In febrile and chaotic scenes on Saturday at the EU’s new migration ground zero, dozens of other migrants clambered over rocks on the shoreline attempting to circumvent border fences.



While four more clung to a rubber ring as they splashed towards the Spanish territory which is the EU’s land frontier with Africa.

Spain says the number of people who have died in the surge has risen to 67.



Early on Saturday morning Moroccan riot police armed with clubs and shields pushed back hundreds of migrants massed close to the border using armoured vehicles.

Soon the mood turned ugly. Migrants began erecting barricades in the street using railings and discarded rubbish bins.



Some still had their rubber rings with them which they had used to swim to Ceuta.

When photographer Ian Whittaker and I tried to take pictures of the mayhem from a hotel balcony we were showered with stones by wild-eyed youngsters.

Thousands had made it to Ceuta on Thursday and Friday but were now leaving after finding little food or no beds for the night.



Most are from Morocco with a smattering from West Africa. Favoured destinations include Britain, France, Spain and the Netherlands.

One Moroccan who had swam to the exclave told me: “We just want a better life but there’s nothing in Ceuta for us.”

Passing the burnt-out shells of a dozen vehicles – including a torched bus – officers herded the migrants back towards the Moroccan coastal town of Fnideq.



Many were bare-foot after discarding their footwear before swimming to Ceuta.

Another said as he left the EU territory: “It’s not good at all, and it’s not fun either. I mean, people are dying here.

“I beg you, please, if you haven’t come yet, don’t come. Don’t do it.”

Yet, minutes later dozens were trying once more to reach the EU. Many, looking barely out of their teens and carrying a few possessions in plastic bags or rucksacks, evaded cops by hugging the rocky shoreline.



Spain’s prime minister Pedro Sanchez blamed Thursday’s 60,000-strong migrant surge on people traffickers.

But some who made the crossing said the Moroccan authorities had encouraged the unpreceendeted surge, the biggest arrival of migranst on EU territory in a single day.

Port city Ceuta – population 84,000 – was soon overwhelmed, leaving locals shellshocked.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he had spoken to Spain’s prime minister and offered “what help we can”.



Public parks became massive open-air dormitories and the beaches were used as lavatories. Charities called it a humanitarian crisis.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Spain sent troops in and the Moroccans flooded their side of the border with security personnel.

At the scene a Madrid-based legal expert told me: “Many of the migrants are going home to rest up. Then they will try again.”

News.title: Man dies before reuniting with wife who he stood by after she hatched poison plot, had him shot & tried to blow him up
News.content:
DYING WISH Man dies before reuniting with wife who he stood by after she hatched poison plot, had him shot & tried to blow him up

A MAN whose final wish was to be reunited with his wife despite her plotting to shoot and poison him has died before she was released from prison.

Ray Weatherall, who was in his early 60s, lost his battle with brain cancer after desperately hoping to survive long enough to see his wife, Hayley, Weatherall freed from her life sentence.



Hayley had tried to murder Ray in 2015 along with her lover, Glenn Pollard – who was also Ray’s best friend.

The dad was diagnosed with brain cancer in 2015 and given 18 months to live, a prognosis that inspired Hayley and Glenn to plot his death.



The pair’s numerous attempts on Ray’s life included shooting him in the face, conspiring to feed him a deadly cocktail of insulin and sleeping pills, and orchestrating a swimming pool heater explosion.

But remarkably survived being shot in the face, a swimming pool heater explosion, and a scheme to kill him with sleeping pills and insulin.



Ray previously revealed that he was “hanging on” until Hayley completed her minimum prison term in seven years’ time.

Now, his family have sadly announced his death on Facebook this week.

Ray’s son Sam, posted a photo of them together captioned: “Fly high Dad”.

Dozens of mourners left tributes, with several relatives changing their profile photos to pictures of Ray with angel and heart emojis.



One comment read, “Heartbreaking. Rest in peace Uncle Ray,” while another described him as “one of life’s heroes.”

The scorned husband, who lived over a decade longer than expected, made 200-mile round trips to visit Hayley every month in prison.

She is still serving a life sentence at HMP Bronzefield in Ashford, Surrey, with a minimum of 15 years.



“There has been no break,” he said previously.

“She gives me a cuddle and a kiss and we sit together, and we always have the family room where it’s got a double sofa.”

“It’s lovely. I wouldn’t want to be not seeing her, let’s put it that way. I’d feel all wrong.”

Hayley and Ray had been together for nine years when the plot took place, after getting married in 2015 shortly before Ray’s diagnosis.

The mum-of-three had then struck up a relationship with Glen, with the pair exchanging naked pictures on WhatsApp.



As well as shooting and poisoning Ray, Hayley also considered pushing him overboard on a fishing trip, a court heard.

The shooting was carried out by Glen’s daughter Heather, 26, in Sandwich, Kent, with the bullet hitting Ray’s cheekbone.

Ray was rolling a cigarette on a break from helping his son Sam cut down a tree when he was blasted with the .22 hunting rifle.



The plot was foiled by detectives who investigated the shooting.

In November 2018, Hayley and the Pollards, of West Stourmouth, Kent, were all convicted at Maidstone Crown Court of conspiracy to murder.

Glen received a life sentence for his part in the crimes, with a minimum of 17 years and Heather a minimum of 15.

Before his death, Ray had described Hayley as the victim in the case, saying she had been brainwashed by Glenn.

He said: “I want her to come back to me.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

When asked if Hayley is still welcome at the family home, the father-of-seven said: “As far as I’m concerned, yes.

“Well, because I love her. And if it weren’t for Mr Pollard, none of this would have ever happened.”

News.title: Greece battling roaring wildfires as violent winds send flames towards Athens as hundreds evacuated across tourist towns
News.content:
FIREFIGHTERS are battling raging wildfires closing in on Athens, with mass evacuations underway across Greece.

Dozens of roaring blazes are being amplified by gale-force winds across several Greek islands, destroying vegetation and burning houses.



On Saturday morning, 29 planes and helicopters began crucial water drops in Viotia, in southern central Greece, where a fire broke out on Friday.

Ground forces, including 18 firefighting units and 92 fire engines, reinforced 325 firefighters as they battled ferocious infernos overnight.





Hundreds are being evacuated by sea from the coastal town after 500 were left stranded.

Another 12 people, fleeing the same blaze, were evacuated from the beach in Porto Germeno by Greek Coast Guard patrol boats.



The huge blaze has now spread to the neighbouring region of Attica, which surrounds the city of Athens.

And firefighters continue to battle a large wildfire on the Greek island of Crete that ignited earlier this week.

Around 8,000 people were ordered to move to safety as flames closed in on southern resort villages, destroying homes, farms, and livestock in their path.

At least three emergency responders have lost their lives during the crisis, including two firefighters who became trapped in their vehicle near the mountain village of Krya Vrysi.



It remains one of the biggest fires currently active on the island and is still burning out of control.

Fires have also broken out on the islands of Paros, Andros and Kalymnos.

Specialist arson investigation teams from the Greek Fire Service have launched formal inquiries into the exact ignition points of the fires.

While investigations are ongoing, extreme heat and weather conditions created the perfect storm for rapid ignition.



It comes amid a spate of deadly wildfires wreaking havoc across Europe – including the UK – as the continent tackles record-breaking heatwaves.

Flames in Spain and France are understood to be dying down, leaving Greece and Turkey to bear the brunt of the soaring temperatures.

There are currently four active fires along Turkey’s Mediterranean coastline, including near the popular tourist centre of Antalya, according to the country’s agricultural ministry.

And hundreds of firefighters battled a blaze near Valpaços in northern Portugal.



The fires have torn through 15,000 hectares so far, news agency Lusa reported, citing officials.

Five people have been injured by the blaze, which has been burning since Tuesday.

In Spain, more than 200,000 hectares of land has burnt in 2026.

A fire in the Ávila region, which has now been stabilised, is now considered the largest recorded wildfire in the nation’s history.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

But, officials are warning there is a high risk of fires re-emerging across most of the country until at least Sunday.

And in Suffolk, hundreds of holidaymakers were evacuated in the middle of the night as a wildfire raced towards a popular seaside resort.

News.title: Ex-Brit Army soldier & Netflix star Nirmal Purja confirmed dead after 10 climbers caught in avalanche in Pakistan
News.content:
'NEVER FORGOTTEN' Ex-Brit Army soldier & Netflix star Nirmal Purja confirmed dead after 10 climbers caught in avalanche in Pakistan

AN ex-Brit Army soldier and Netflix star is among ten people who have been killed in a deadly avalanche.

Nirmal “Nimsdai” Purja, 43, had been leading a mountaineering group through one of the world’s tallest mountains in Pakistan when disaster struck.



The hikers had been scaling a particularly dangerous part of the 26,414ft mountain when an avalanche struck at around midday on Thursday.

The group completely lost contact with the team back at base, sparking a frantic rescue mission.





Four bodies were found on Friday but now all ten climbers are confirmed dead.

They include famed mountaineer Kili Pemba Sherpa, who has summitted Everest 21 times, Omani mountaineer Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy, Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung and American climber Mallory Geis.



A Chinese national, Pakistani national and two more Nepalese climbers were also killed.

In a chilling twist, the Netflix star revealed that he had changed the route last minute.

In one of his final posts, he wrote that the last-minute change had been made in an attempt to “become the FIRST person in history to climb all 14 eight-thousanders twice” without oxygen.

Broad Peak Mountain is one of the toughest in the world to climb.

Former reality TV star Spencer Matthews previously posted about the missing persons, saying “we pray for a miracle”.



He has now shared a tribute to his friend and co-star, saying that the loss is “heartbreaking”.

Brit TV adventurer Bear Grylls has also paid tribute to the climber, writing on Instagram: “Heartbreaking news for so many climbers around the world who had a relationship with this remarkable and unique man. We will never forget you Nims and your unstoppable spirit.”

Nimsdai and Bear Grylls worked with Matthews to recover the body of his brother who was the youngest Brit to summit Everest.



Elite Exped, the company that organised the mountain treks, also published a statement in tribute to the lost lives.

They wrote on Instagram: “It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nimsdai tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak.

“Our deepest thoughts, prayers and heartfelt condolences are with their families, friends and loved ones. No words can ease the pain of this unimaginable loss, and we ask that everyone respects their privacy as they grieve.”

They finished the post with a heartbreaking promise: “You will never be forgotten; your spirit, your purpose and your legacy will continue to inspire generations to come.”

Nimsdai is one of the world’s best-known mountaineers.



He shot to global fame after climbing all 14 of the world’s mountains higher than 8,000 metres in just 189 days, smashing the previous record.

The astonishing feat was documented in the Netflix film “14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Before becoming a professional climber, Nimsdai served for six years in the elite Gurkha regiment before spending a decade with the UK’s Special Boat Service.

In 2018, he was awarded an MBE by Queen Elizabeth II for exceptional military service in high-risk environments.

News.title: ‘Alpha male’ boxer killed grandad, 62, with one punch in unprovoked attack & left him for dead as kids watched in horror
News.content:
A FORMER boxer killed a grandad with one punch in an unprovoked attack and left him for dead as kids watched on in horror.

James “Jim” McKeown was found lying on the ground by a member of the public in Beaumont Leys Park, Leicestershire, on April 6.



The 62-year-old had been walking home from a nearby pub when he was viciously assaulted by Joshua Moore, 34, who was riding a quad bike in the park with a young child.

Moore had confronted Mr McKeown and punched him in the face where he fell to the ground and hit his head on the pavement.



He then placed Mr McKeown in the recovery position before fleeing the park without contacting emergency services.

He was raced to Royal Leicester Infirmary but despite the best efforts of medical staff, he died a short time later.

Moore was jailed for five years and nine months after pleading guilty to manslaughter at Leicester Crown Court earlier this month.

CCTV footage released by Leicestershire Police show Moore returning to the scene an hour later telling an officer: “I hit him”.



The force said later how Moore clearly thought “it was more important to sort out his affairs” before calling 999.

They added he went as far as cancelling a tattoo appointment he had booked for the next day.

The court heard how Mr McKeown had been found by a passer-by in a pool of his own blood, reports ITV.

Moore is said to have told cops he had struck Mr McKeown in “self-defence” but this was dismissed by prosecutors.

Sentencing Moore on his 34th birthday, Judge Timothy Spencer told him “there is more than an element of you wanting to be the alpha male”.



He said: “You could simply have ridden on, you could have avoided him, you could have avoided any exchange of words.

“A truly big man would have done just that. But no, you decided to punch him, with these devastating consequences.”

Marie de Redman, defending Moore, said the killer was “truly sorry” for what had happened.



Judge Spencer said that Moore had “never sought to shirk responsibility” but said he was “far too quick with your fists”, labelling Moore’s blows as “powerful and devastating”.

He added that the “attack was committed in the presence of children” and Moore had “simply abandoned” Mr McKeown as he lay unconscious on the ground.

Moore’s previous conviction was also a factor in his sentence after he was jailed for eight years for a burglary in 2016 where he had assaulted another victim.

Following the incident, Mr McKeown’s family paid tribute saying: “We have lost a loving father, brother, partner and grandfather, our lives will never be the same again.

“Jimmy has lived locally for nearly 20 years and was well known in the community, affectionately known to many as Spider,” they added.



Detective Inspector Kevin Hames from East Midlands Special Operations Unit (EMSOU) Murder Investigation Team, said: “Sadly, this is a tragic death that could have been avoided. Moore had a choice that day and should have walked away, without using any violence, Jim posed no threat to him.

“His actions have now left a family devastated at the loss of their loved one.

“The fact that he didn’t make any attempt to contact the emergency services following the incident shows exactly what type of man he is.

“He placed Jim in the recovery position and clearly saw the injuries he had caused but that didn’t stop him from riding away, returning home to organise his affairs before handing himself in.

“Notwithstanding this was a totally unprovoked attack, Joshua Moore should not have been riding a quad bike in the park in the first place.



“While we are pleased that Moore has admitted to being responsible for Jim’s death, there are certainly no winners in the case.

“Jim’s family now face a life without him, and nothing can replace the feeling of that loss. They have shown immense bravery throughout the investigation and subsequent legal proceedings. This has in no way been easy for them.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Moore now faces a lengthy term in prison, and I hope it gives him the opportunity to reflect on his actions.

“I would also like to thank the community of West Leicester for their support in the investigation and thank the members of the community who unlike Joshua Moore, stopped to provide care to Jim.”

News.title: Naples earthquake live: Italy struck by 4.7 magnitude quake as rocks crush cars
News.content:
Residents in Naples have been left terrified after a powerful earthquake caused damage to the Italian city - it registered at 4.7 magnitude

A powerful earthquake has struck southern Italy, causing damage in the city of Naples.

The 4.7 magnitude quake has left neighbourhoods without power, and residents are taking to the streets in fear. It occurred just before 8pm (local time).

According to data released by the INGV (National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology), the magnitude was 4.7. Power outages have been reported from Pizzofalcone to Fuorigrotta, and there has been a massive landslide in Pozzuoli.

Images show buildings have crumbled, with debris crushing cars.

News.title: Amanda Knox to do Edinburgh Fringe comedy over jail for Meredith Kercher death
News.content:
Amanda Knox to do Edinburgh Fringe comedy over jail for Meredith Kercher death

Amanda Knox was acquitted after being jailed for the murder of British foreign exchange student Meredith Kercher in Perugia, Italy, in 2007, and now she will share her story on stage

View 2 Images Amanda Knox is to do a stand-up comedy at the Edinburgh Fringe (Image: Getty Images)

Amanda Knox will perform a stand-up comedy show at Edinburgh Fringe about her wrongful imprisonment for the murder of Meredith Kercher.

‌



British foreign exchange student Meredith was killed in Perugia, Italy, in 2007, with her American roommate Ms Knox and her then-boyfriend, Raffaele Sollecito, arrested and convicted of murder and sexual assault in 2009.

‌



The couple maintained their innocence and, after years of legal battles, were acquitted of sexual assault and murder by Italy’s highest court in 2015.

‌



Just over a decade on, Ms Knox is now set to share her story on stage.

View 2 Images Amanda Knox speaking at event in London last April (Image: Andy Lines / Daily Mirror)

Donald Trump gives curt answer to question about Gianni Infantino's FIFA World Cup selloff READ MORE :

Ms Knox, 39, is now married with two children and lives on Vashon-Maury Island in rural Washington. She said she initially planned to make a show about motherhood – but was told by comedian friends she had to “address the elephant in the room”.

‌



Her comedy show’s title Cartwheel references a story that once claimed she did cartwheels in the police station after her friend’s death.

Speaking to The Telegraph, Ms Knox said she did not believe there were any topics off bounds for comedy, but insisted she would not poke fun at Ms Kercher’s death.

“I don’t joke about Meredith’s death. I joke a lot about how I was vilified, but I don’t joke about her murder. That’s just a line for me. I set red lines for myself that other comedians don’t. I’ve had other comedians pitch me jokes that I just would not do,” she said.

‌



Asked about whether her loved ones were concerned about backlash to the show, she referred to a gag she says on stage: “My friends and family are actually really nervous for me, despite my spotless record in the court of public opinion.”

However, The Telegraph has reported that Ms Kercher’s relatives, according to their lawyer Francesco Maresca, have called the idea of the show “offensive and deplorable”.

Ms Knox said: “If they reached out to me and actually communicated with me for the first time ever, I would absolutely want to talk to them. Something that is an unresolved wound for me is the fact that I have never been able to talk to them. I assume they still assume that I’m guilty. I would very much want to establish that kind of communication, but I’m not going to have my life dictated by what they want for me.”

Article continues below

She added: “We share a grief, and we both knew a real person who died, and who primarily belongs to them, but I’m a person too. I have the life that I have lived, and I have the right to tell my own story, and Meredith is a big part of that story. And I think I honour her.”

Ms Knox said that she believed Ms Kercher would “appreciate the show because it grapples with what it means to be a young woman, and it is honest”, adding that she thought her late roommate would have found it “funny”.

Ms Knox has previously shared her story in documentaries, an eight-part TV drama she produced with Monica Lewinsky, and books. Rudy Hermann Guede was convicted of Ms Kercher’s murder in 2008. He was released from prison in 2021 after serving 13 years of a 16-year term.

News.title: Prince Louis marks milestone at Commonwealth Games as he joins William and Kate in packed stadium
News.content:
Prince Louis marks milestone at Commonwealth Games as he joins William and Kate in packed stadium

A bored looking Prince Louis was snapped in a rare public appearance alongside his siblings and Prince William and Princess Kate for the kids' first official visit to Scotland

View 4 Images The Prince and Princess of Wales with their kids at the Commonwealth Games (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

Prince Louis is attending his first major sporting event this afternoon, as he joined the Prince and Princess of Wales and his siblings to watch Netball at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

‌



The family of five took their seats in a packed stadium for the semi final clash between Australia and Jamaica, with the children sandwiched between the Prince and Princess of Wales.

‌



Kensington Palace announced that the Duke and Duchess of Rothesay, as they are known in Scotland, would be attending the penultimate day of the so-called "friendly games" this morning.

‌



View 4 Images Prince Louis with his head in his hands at the netball match (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Despite this, the appearances of Prince George, 13, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Louis, eight, was kept under wraps. It marks the first time the children have been publicly seen in Scotland.

Louis, who is famous for his playful antics and his unfiltered facial expressions, regularly attends set-piece royal events such as the Christmas and Easter church services and Trooping the Colour, but he has only ever attended one public engagement.

‌



View 4 Images Prince William speaking to Prince Louis and Prince George (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

This was in May 2023 as part of the King’s Coronation celebrations, where he joined his parents and siblings at a Big Help Out volunteering initiative.

His appearance at the Commonwealth Games today also marks the first time little Louis has attended a major sporting fixture, as unlike his older siblings who frequently join their parents at key football and tennis matches such as the Euros and Wimbledon, Louis has yet to join them.

‌



View 4 Images Princess Charlotte, Prince Louis and Prince George during the Netball Semi-Final match at The Hydro (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

His appearance today therefore marks a major milestone for the young royal, and he looked delighted to take a seat inside the 5,000 seater Hydro for the second semi final in the Women’s Netball.

The family of five were warmly welcomed inside the arena, as they looked forward to a tense match between the World’s No 1 team Australia and Birmingham 2022 silver medalists, Jamaica.

‌



Later on Saturday, William and Catherine will spend time with Team Wales athletes and their families.

Before the games the future King chatted to five Team Wales athletes – lawn and indoor bowler Ross Owen, blind para bowler Julie Thomas and her guide John Wilson, and weightlifters Madaline Connelly and Catrin Haf Jones – when he visited the London Welsh School in Hanwell, west London.

The royal couple will also spend time with athletes competing at the games whose careers have been empowered by the charity SportsAid, which Catherine has supported as patron since 2013, and meet emerging talent taking part in the Team England Futures project.

‌



Sporting stars whose early promise was boosted by SportsAid include Sir Chris Hoy, Ellie Simmonds, Dame Jessica Ennis-Hill and Tom Daley.

The Commonwealth Games, affectionately known as “the friendly games”, started on July 23, following a spectacular Opening Ceremony that saw the King and Queen emerge from Doctor Who ’s Tardis.

Over the nine days of action so far, the Duke and Duchess of Edinburgh and the Princess Royal have attended several days of the sporting action.

Article continues below

William and Catherine visited the Games the last time it was held in Glasgow in 2014, accompanied by the prince’s younger brother, Prince Harry.

News.title: Tragic Brianna Ghey's mum launches phones down summer holidays challenge with plea to kids
News.content:
Tragic Brianna Ghey's mum launches phones down summer holidays challenge with plea to kids

EXCLUSIVE: Esther Ghey, whose girl Brianna was murdered by two teens, is challenging youngsters to put their phones down for a week this summer and play outdoors with friends

View 4 Images Esther is urging young people to go phone free (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/REX/Shutterstock)

She's tirelessly called on the government to protect kids online after her girl Brianna’s brutal murder - b ut now Esther Ghey is urging youngsters to take the matter into their own hands – by going phone free for a week this summer holidays.

‌



Esther hopes her Phone’s Down Challenge will encourage children to play outdoors and have fun with their friends. She told the Mirror: "Before her death, Brianna was completely addicted to her phone and social media.

‌



"This challenge is a chance for us all to be more mindful of how much we use our phones and give kids the opportunity to break the habit and experience some of the summer holidays in the real world."

‌



View 4 Images Brianna's murder was planned on Snapchat (Image: PA)

Brianna Ghey and Lucy Harrison's mums united in agony of losing their daughters READ MORE :

Brianna, 16, was stabbed to death by 15-year-old’s Scarlett Jenkinson and Eddie Ratcliffe, who planned the horror on social media app Snapchat.

Among young people inspired to take part in the challenge is Olivia Bell, 13, who has deleted TikTok, Instagram and gaming app Roblox for seven days. She said: “I decided to take part because I’m on my phone too much, maybe 4-6 hours a day when I’m not at school. I’m currently on day three and I’ve found it quite difficult because I have to keep myself entertained.

‌



“But, a friend came round yesterday [and] we had so much fun. There were no phones at all – we had such good conversations, played football, and practiced our scripts for a Matilda show we’re both doing. When the challenge finishes, we’re planning to do no phone Saturdays as a family.”

View 4 Images Esther hopes the challenge will get youngsters outdoors (Image: Brianna Ghey Legacy Project)

Olivia’s mum Debbie added: “It was lovely listening to them in the garden playing football – for me that’s what summer is all about.” Olivia is completing the quest with pal Charlotte, 13, who said: [TO COME]

‌



It comes as research by The Children's Commissioner found one in five young people spend over seven hours a day on screens, easily exceeding 35 hours a week. It also showed screen time severely damages and disrupts children's sleep patterns.

The government last month announced a landmark plan to ban children under 16 from accessing major social media platforms by spring 2027. The policy will likely include an under-16 social media ban for platforms like TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat, Facebook, X, and YouTube.

View 4 Images Olivia Bell often spends 4-6 hours a day on her phone (Image: Brianna Ghey Legacy Project/BBC Breakfast)

Article continues below

Restrictions for 16 and 17-year-olds, including overnight app curfews from midnight to 6am and default-off personalised feeds. And strict age minimums of 18 for romantic AI companion chatbots.

News.title: Urgent manhunt launched as prisoner escapes from transport vehicle outside court
News.content:
Urgent manhunt launched as prisoner escapes from transport vehicle outside court

Stephen Grzyb, 22, from the West Derby/Dovecot area of Liverpool, was being transported from Belle Vale custody suite to Liverpool Magistrates Court when he escaped

View Image Stephen Grzyb has escaped as he was being taken to court (Image: Merseyside Police)

Police are hunting for a wanted man who has escaped a prison van on the way to court.

Stephen Grzyb, 22, from the West Derby/Dovecot area of Liverpool, was being transported from Belle Vale custody suite to Liverpool Magistrates Court in the city centre by GEOAmey, a prisoner transport contractor, when he managed to get away.

He fled from the van when it arrived outside court at around 10am, running down Red Cross Street in the direction of The Strand.

Grzyb was being transported to court after being charged with a domestic-related burglary. He is described as white with short dark hair and when last seen was wearing a navy T-shirt and navy shorts.

Merseyside Police said: "We are appealing for information to find a wanted man following his escape from the custody of a prisoner transport contractor in Liverpool city centre today (Saturday 1 August).

"At around 10am, the man - who was being transported from Belle Vale custody suite by GEOAmey - made off on arrival outside Liverpool Magistrates Court.

"He made off on foot down Red Cross Street in the direction of The Strand. Extensive enquiries are currently being taken by officers to locate him. Patrols have also attended the home of the alleged victim in the case to ensure she is safeguarded while the search is ongoing.

"The man is Stephen Grzyb, 22 years, of Princess Drive, Liverpool who was charged with a domestic-related burglary. Grzyb is described as white with short dark hair and when last seen was wearing a navy T-shirt and navy shorts."

T/Inspector Bethan Hannon said: "We understand the concern this incident will cause, and it is vital the public can see Grzyb's face so they can report any sightings and help us bring him back into custody as soon as possible.

Article continues below

“If you have heard from him or know where he is, please do the right thing and come forward. Assisting him in any way will bring police to your own door, so it is not an association worth keeping. If you see Grzyb, please call 999 immediately. We are carrying out extensive enquiries to find him with patrols on foot and CCTV enquiries being made right across the city centre so that we can return him to custody.”

The statement from the force adds: "Call 999 if you see him. You can also contact Merseyside Police social media desk via X and Facebook @MerPolCC, via our website: https://www.merseyside.police.uk/ro/report/ocr/af/how-to-report-a-crime/ or call 101 quoting incident reference 26000615520.

"Alternatively, contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111, or via their website here: https://crimestoppers-uk.org/give-information/forms/give-information-anonymously."

News.title: Andy Burnham urges new Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig 'to go further and do more' after by-election win
News.content:
Andy Burnham urges new Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig 'to go further and do more' after by-election win

Labour candidate Bev Craig won the largest by-election in British history to succeed Andy Burnham after defeating Reform's Sian Astley in the second round of votes

View 2 Images Andy Burnham spoke at a victory rally with Bev Craig (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

Andy Burnham has urged his successor as Greater Manchester mayor to “go further and do more” after her by-election win.

‌



Labour candidate Bev Craig won the largest by-election in British history to succeed Mr Burnham in the job after he quit and became PM.

‌



The result came late on Friday night, and represents yet another electoral defeat for Nigel Farage's Reform party.

‌



Speaking at a victory event in Manchester alongside Ms Craig, Mr Burnham dubbed her “queen of the north”

He said: “You are the right person to lead this great city region forward into its best decade ever, because that is what the next decade is going to be.

View 2 Images Bev Craig won with 309,525 votes (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

‌



“So, ladies and gentlemen, without any further ado, can you give it up for the queen of the north, the new Mayor of Greater Manchester, Bev Craig.”

The 41-year-old leader of Manchester City Council won in a run-off with Reform's Sian Astley after no candidate won more than 50% of the vote.

Turnout in the race was just over 25% - down on the last mayoral contest in the region - with more than 500,000 ballots cast out of an eligible two million voters taking part. After the run-off vote, taking into account voters' second preferences, Ms Craig achieved 309,525 of the votes.

‌



She told supporters the public have been “crying out” for a commitment from “people in power that get it”.

Ms Craig said: “(People) that want to put more money in their pockets. That want to make life easier, that are on their side, and I’m excited to get stuck i.

“I’ll also say one final thing, and that’s about what people have voted for in this election.

Article continues below

“They voted for Greater Manchester to build on the legacy that we’ve created together, but they voted to reject the division and the dividing lines that people put in our communities.”

Analysis of the full votes showed that Ms Craig topped the poll in the first round of voting in all the 10 local authority areas that make up Greater Manchester.

Ms Astley came second in eight of the 10 areas while Green candidate Geraldine Coggins came second in Manchester and the Conservative candidate Phil Eckersley was second in Trafford.

News.title: Andy Burnham urged to bring in supporters ownership model amid FIFA controversy
News.content:
Andy Burnham urged to bring in supporters ownership model amid FIFA controversy

EXCLUSIVE: The Co-operative Party - Labour's sister Party - is calling for a new organisation, a Supporters Direct 2.0, to back supporter and community ownership across sport

View 2 Images Andy Burnham has been urged to help supporters fight back against private ownership (Image: VCG via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has been urged to help fight back against a “fundamentally broken” sports ownership model with a new organisation to hand power back to supporters.

‌



The Co-operative Party - Labour's sister Party - is calling for a new body, a Supporters Direct 2.0, to back supporter and community ownership across sport.

‌



In a new report, they say this would help clubs across all sports with legal, governance and development support, reducing the power of private finance.

‌



It comes amid a row over FIFA proposals to sell a stake in the World Cup. The governing body had launched a consultation over setting up a separate $20billion (£14.9billion) company to run its competitions, only to U-turn after a furious backlash.

View 2 Images Andy Burnham weighed in on the FIFA controversy and called for Gianni Infantino to quit (Image: Getty Images)

The report brands English football a “global commercial success story”, but that it has created an imbalance where “supporters provide the loyalty, culture and community identity which give clubs their value”, but ownership and decision-making remains concentrated in the hands of a “small number of private interests”.

‌



It highlights that most Premier League clubs are privately-owned by international owners, such as hedge funds and private equity firms, and argues for more community ownership instead.

The Co-op Party says the attempts at selling off World Cup shares should be a warning about the state of sport ownership and the need for change

There have also been a series of issues in Rugby Union, with London Irish falling into administration in 2023, following Worcester and Wasps also folding. Speaking at the time, RFU chairman Tom llube blamed “unsustainable business models” for the clubs failing, adding that all three “have had fragile business models for many years”.

‌



In Rugby league this year, six teams have faced financial issues, with Keighley, Salford Red Devils, Featherstone Rovers, Halifax Panthers and North Wales Crusaders all going bust.

In cricket, Yorkshire's chief executive Sanjay Patel is trying to end 163 years of being a members-run club, and claiming failing to do so could see them miss out on test matches.

General Secretary of the Co-operative Party Joe Fortune said: “The World Cup fiasco of the past week is an extreme version of what already exists: private ownership across sport which comes at the expense of fans.

‌



“The Co-op Party says private ownership dominates across sport - with several rugby league clubs in administration and efforts to demutualise Yorkshire Cricket.

"We want to see a shift in power to the people who are at the heart of sport. A new Supporters Direct would allow supporters and communities to take control of the clubs they love.”

The first Labour and Co-operative Prime Minister in history, Mr Burnham was previously chairman of Supporters Direct - an organisation set up to increase supporter voice and ownership in football.

Article continues below

Speaking in the 2000s on the issue, he said: “I have always believed that football clubs belong more to their supporters than their shareholders. Some people have bits of paper to say they own a clubs’ assets – stadium, training ground, brand – but the heart and soul of every club is the property of its fans.”

News.title: 'Bright' woman, 22, died after nurse failed to carry out checks as ordered then lied
News.content:
'Bright' woman, 22, died after nurse failed to carry out checks as ordered then lied

A nurse claimed she had checked on Amy Barber every five minutes at a psychiatric ward but the 22-year-old was found unresponsive 25 minutes later

View 3 Images Amy Barber with her mum Sue (Image: LIVERPOOL ECHO)

The devastated mother of a young woman who died in hospital paid tribute to her girl after a nurse was found guilty of wilfully neglecting her on the night of her death.

‌



Amy Barber had been diagnosed with emotionally unstable personality disorder and an eating disorder at the age of 14. She was transferred to Brooklands Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit, inside the Clatterbridge Hospital in Wirral, years later after a record of self harm during her teen years.

‌



Amy was due to be checked on every five minutes by staff at the ward but on June 30, 2022, Amy was found unresponsive in her room.

‌



View 3 Images Amy was 22 years old when she died (Image: LIVERPOOL ECHO)

Registered mental health nurse Laurence Tchapong was in charge of checking on Amy that night and handed her a towel at 8.15pm before leaving. Another nurse, handing out medication at the time, entered Amy's room and found her unresponsive 25 minutes later.

Tchapong, who had been working for an agency at the time, was assigned to do "level two checks" which included checking on patients through the window of their bedroom every five minutes, according to the Liverpool Echo. The nurse, from Manchester, was also supposed to see if the patient was awake and to check for signs of self harm.

‌



CCTV showed Tchapong handing Amy the towel at 8.15pm and Liverpool Crown Court heard another nurse Victoria Connelly had gone to Amy's room at 8.40pm to give her medication but found the 22-year-old unresponsive. Ms Connelly raised the alarm and Amy was taken to Arrowe Park Hospital but she suffered serious brain injured and sadly died on July 4, 2022. Amy had taken her life.

View 3 Images Laurence Tchapong leaving Liverpool Crown Court (Image: LIVERPOOL ECHO)

Tchapong had signed at least 10 observation entries that night and said she saw Amy awake but CCTV footage revealed this hadn't happened. The nurse had also put down an entry at 8.55pm with a possible question mark and signed it. The nurse later, in a meeting with her superior Gill Judson, claimed the patient asked for an apple at 8.40pm then for a towel five minutes after, so the nurse went to get those items. Tchapong claimed the next thing she knew was the alarms in the ward going off.

‌



The nurse was also asked about the 8.55pm log but reportedly became distressed. The superior also spoke to Tchapong later and said the nurse recalled the same events but added Amy has been stood brushing her teeth at 8.50pm. On the 8.55pm log the nurse said she understood it looked like an 'A' for awake but had put down a question mark instead, as CPR was being performed on the patient.

Tchapong was found guilty of wilfully neglecting Amy Barber after a trial at Liverpool Crown Court, according to the ECHO. The nurse's defence said Tchapong accepted she had not checked on Amy after 8.15pm but said this was due to other tasks and other patients. Tchapong is due to be sentenced on September 1.

Mum Sue, 59, from Nantwich, shared an emotional tribute to her daughter and said: "She was amazing, she was bright, kind, funny and crazily clever. She got 11 A*s at GCSE and then she got stuck in the mental health system. She was fantastic, I know every mother says that but people would tell me the same thing, she really was.

‌



"She ran with the Olympic torch in 2012 and was a registered organ donor so after her death she has helped four people." Sue added: "We were as close as a mother and daughter can be. Amy was my person."

On Tchapong, the mum said: "Amy was poorly but she wasn't checked on for 25 minutes. She was on five minute checks, which doesn't mean five past, 10 past, but it means she needs to be constantly checked on."

The mum added: "She was doing other things rather than looking after my daughter. I hope she gets a decent punishment. We've had to listen to Amy's last hour over and over again during the trial because she pleaded not guilty."

Article continues below

When life is difficult, Samaritans are available day or night, 365 days a year. You can call them for free on 116 123 or visit samaritans.org

News.title: Sir John Curtice: The 'Burnham bounce' is real but it's not massive
News.content:
But with still no more than a narrow lead over Reform, it is unsurprising Burnham has ruled out an early election. In any event, Reform's displacement from first place in the polls for the first time in over a year appears to owe more to its own difficulties than it does to Labour's new-found popularity.

Reform has been dogged in recent weeks by questions about the legality of the source of some of its funding and about whether Farage should have declared to the Commons authorities some of the funding he received before being elected an MP. Following these allegations, Farage announced on 7 July that he was standing down and putting himself again before the voters of his Clacton constituency in a by-election now scheduled for 13 August.

This move appears to have backfired. Immediately before Farage's announcement, Reform's average poll rating stood at 27%. In the polls conducted immediately after Farage's announcement, it fell by three points to 24%, the level at which it still stands now, and the lowest it has been for 15 months. At the same time, Farage's personal poll ratings are now the worst they have been since he returned as Reform's leader during the 2024 election campaign.

News.title: The five dramatic days that shook Infantino and world football
News.content:
The question many have asked around Infantino's plan is tied into a separate - but critical - aspect of the fundamental reasons behind this week unravelling.

Fifa is a not-for-profit organisation. It has huge financial reserves - over $2bn (Â£1.48bn) - and is expected to announce record revenues of about $15bn (Â£11.13bn) in relation to this summer's World Cup.

Given that backdrop - and the reality some countries simply did not need the extra $40m (Â£29.67m) being offered for football development initiatives if they signed up to Infantino's plan by 19 September - many wondered why private investment was needed in the first place.

It was a question that needed to be asked. But that did not happen in public - or, it has become apparent, privately in Fifa's corridors of power.

Many of Fifa's most senior people - from vice-presidents to special advisers and executives - did not have a chance to ask any questions, simply because they had no clue the plans were being drawn up.

Uefa had strongly opposed the plans from the moment they became public. When they were dropped, its response was damning.

"The current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family," it said in a statement.

"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of Fifa's member associations to elect him as their president in 2016, he said: 'Of course we have to be transparent.'

"He told the assembled stakeholders: 'The money of Fifa is your money. It's not the money of the Fifa president. You are the national associations and the money of Fifa has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver."

It was not the first time a lack of transparency had been highlighted.

Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa - president of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), and one of eight Fifa vice-presidents - referred to it too.

He said any future plans that may impact global football should be presented to members "in a timely, transparent and meaningful manner".

"The future of global football must always be shaped through proper consultation, collective dialogue and respect for the established governance structures of our game," he added.

Football Australia chair Anter Isaac said trust was earned "not simply through good decisions, but through the integrity of the processes that lead to them".

"Football has never stood still, nor should it," he said.

"Some principles, however, should never change. Integrity. Independence. Good governance. Transparency. Meaningful consultation. Due process. These are not constraints on progress."

News.title: Faisal Islam: Four reasons why the World Cup plan never stacked up
News.content:
In the slides, Fifa's central argument was that football does not raise enough cash in relation to its fan base, that "Fifa has been under-monetised versus other leagues" and so "global football development gets squeezed".

It did this with reference to a comparative chart showing annual revenue as well as revenue per fan for Fifa, the Uefa Champions League, Premier League, US baseball and NFL American football.

On the face of it, Fifa is the poorer cousin at just $1 per global fan, compared to NFL's $52.80. But this measure is rather suspect.

The World Cup is not an annual competition - it happens once every four years. If instead this was done on revenue per World Cup 2026 match, Fifa makes multiples of the Premier League, perhaps more than three times as much.

As important, football is decentralised globally, so more of the revenues go to individual leagues, such as the Premier League or Champions League. Fifa was effectively arguing it wanted to keep more of that overall football pie.

Football's fans are also spread across the globe, in rich and poor countries alike. NFL has a much smaller base concentrated in the US and is pretty much the whole of American Football.

Finally, about half of NFL's revenues are paid out as wages. Fifa does not pay Erling Haaland or Lionel Messi or Vozinha. Profits would have yielded a rather different result than the chartâs focus on revenues.

News.title: Infantino on the brink? Who might replace him if he goes?
News.content:
Life moves fast for Fifa president Gianni Infantino.

It was doing so last month as he was zig-zagging across the United States in a private jet to make him virtually omnipresent as the World Cup reached its crescendo.

On 19 July he must have felt on top of the world as, together with US President Donald Trump, they handed the trophy over to Spain.

Less than two weeks later, Infantino is in a lonely place after scrapping controversial plans to sell off stakes in Fifa competitions to private investment.

Condemned by UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, castigated by fans of the game he professes to want to protect. These can easily be deflected as hazards of the job.

Less so the threatened boycott of Fifa competitions by European governing body Uefa, and its subsequent stunning statement in which it declared it had lost confidence in Infantino's leadership.

Concacaf (North and Central America and the Caribbean) and the AFC (Asia) also - in their own ways - have offered withering assessments of how Fifa is being run under Infantino.

"This issue extends far beyond a single proposal," said the AFC. "Rather, it has exposed fundamental weaknesses in Fifa's consultation and decision-making processes that must now be addressed."

Sources say, in addition to rejecting Infantino's plan, the vast majority of the Concacaf members are either losing faith in the Fifa president's ability to govern the game, or have lost it altogether.

On top of that, Carlos Cordeiro, special adviser to Infantino and appointed by Trump as senior adviser to the White House Task Force on the 2026 World Cup, has resigned.

Fifa's chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said in a statement to Associated Press that Fifa's own administration was "deceived" about the project.

BBC Sport has approached Fifa for comment.

It feels as though the walls are closing in on Infantino.

But if this is the beginning of the end of his tenure, who takes over?

News.title: He thought a fitness supplement was safe, but it sent him into psychosis
News.content:
Daniel Murphy thought he was taking a safe and tested dietary supplement that would help him put on muscle in the gym.

But over the following two years, his mental health spiralled to such a degree he ended up in a state of psychosis in which he believed his wife was trying to steal his business and his mother-in-law was going to kill him.

Unknown to Daniel, the daily pills he had been taking had been mixed with testosterone.

The 32-year-old is one of 54,000 consumers listed in a case against a multimillion-pound peptide company based in the US, which sold its products around the world.

The owner of Paradigm Peptides, Matthew Kawa, was jailed for five years and 10 months on Thursday after he admitted deliberately selling unapproved medicines, trying to deceive people about what they were and illegally bringing the products into the country.

His sister, Jennifer Stechkober, who also pleaded guilty to selling unapproved medicines, was sent to prison for a year and four months.

Both admitted they had lied about where the pills were sourced, their purity and their company's testing procedures. Despite claiming the supplements were manufactured in the US, they were actually imported from China, India and several other countries. The pair also faked certificates of analysis, the documents that prove the safety and quality of a product.

Paradigm Peptides' website had stated it "stringently" tested all their products to ensure "efficacy, purity and potency", but the pair admitted not testing or analysing any of the products they sold, so they had not been aware they had been mixed with testosterone.

News.title: What is Iran's Pickaxe Mountain and why does Trump say he wants to bomb it?
News.content:
US President Donald Trump has repeatedly threatened to bomb a suspected underground nuclear site in Iran known as Pickaxe Mountain, where recent satellite images appear to show construction work taking place.

Pickaxe Mountain is one of the few Iranian sites linked to the country's nuclear programme that has not been the target of US and Israeli strikes. There have been unproven claims that some of Iran's stock of highly enriched uranium may be kept there, which could be further enriched for use in nuclear weapons.

"We'll be hitting that area pretty soon, and very heavily," Trump told reporters on 21 July. And on 28 July he said: "I know exactly what's going on at Pickaxe. It's not a big problem - we took out their nuclear sites, and we'll have to take out Pickaxe if we don't make a deal."

Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said on 22 July that "no nuclear activity is taking place" at Pickaxe Mountain, and described US threats as "a fabricated pretext for aggression, destruction, and sabotage".

BBC Verify and BBC Persian have spoken to experts and analysed satellite imagery to piece together what we know about the site, and the potential impact of any strike.

News.title: Decades-long search ends with discovery of new marine species
News.content:
The Great Barrier Reef might be the world's most famous underwater ecosystem, but hidden in UK waters lies an ancient marine world you may not have heard of.

Known as maerl beds, these carpets of coral-like seaweed create some of the richest habitats in the sea.

And 40 years ago, while studying one such bed for her PhD, Prof Christine Maggs found a fragment of pink-striped seaweed living on maerl she had never seen before.

The discovery would become a lifelong obsession and a decades-long scientific puzzle.

News.title: Former workers fight for wages they say they're owed: 'It makes me sick'
News.content:
What happens when your boss is also the HR department, the grievance handler and the person deciding whether you get paid?

"I just want my wages. It's my hard work. I just want what I'm owed."

Sonia Garcia Monuz is one of several workers trying to recover money she believes she is owed by a catering firm based in Berkshire.

Latest figures show early conciliation cases involving unpaid wages rose by about 17% between 2024 and 2025, according to Acas â the independent body that helps resolve workplace disputes.

Acas says nearly half of hospitality workers, 49%, experience problems at work.

News.title: Greater Manchester mayor says Burnham's new powers will change lives
News.content:
Greater Manchester's new Mayor Bev Craig has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham's move to give the regions more power could "change our lives".

The Labour candidate claimed victory in Thursday's by-election after securing 309,525 votes over Reform's Sian Astley, who won 157,178.

The 41-year-old will succeed Burnham as mayor, after he stood down to run in the Makerfield by-election in June. The pair appeared together at a Labour rally in Manchester after Craig's election win.

Craig said: "For a prime minister two weeks in, to start giving powers out of Whitehall and putting it in the places that can make a difference - that can change our lives."

She added: "I will rise to his challenge about taking the power and control that he is offering mayors like me to make our regions better.

"Because that is what it is all about."

News.title: Stick to spending limits, PM and chancellor tell ministers in joint memo
News.content:
Healey said the budget would "meet our fiscal rules" and "give businesses and families some of the stability they need to plan for the future".

A report in the Times says the joint letter told ministers they must work "within the budgets they have already got" even while "pay[ing] for new things they want to do this year and next".

While the ongoing war in Iran is pushing up inflation and borrowing costs, senior Treasury sources confirmed that the government was determined to stay "well within the fiscal rules" inherited from Sir Keir and Reeves.

But Burnham has said his government will stick to Labour's fiscal rules on spending and borrowing as well as the party's 2024 manifesto pledges not to increase income tax, VAT or National Insurance contributions.

He also said he will honour the fiscal rules imposed by Reeves, which include a pledge to balance day-to-day spending with tax revenues by the end of the decade.

An influential think tank said earlier this week that the prime minister only had a small margin of error to do this and that Healey may have to cut spending or raise taxes to meet Burnham's policy priorities, such as extra defence spending and better social care.

Healey was defence secretary under Sir Keir but resigned after a row over defence spending commitments, saying he was "certain" that Britain should lift its spending to 3% by 2030.

Questioned about funding on Thursday, Burnham's Defence Secretary Wes Streeting repeatedly refused to commit to that target.

"Before we set out specific spending commitments, we will also set out how we pay for them at the same time," he said.

Reeves left a Â£22bn buffer in her last Budget, but persistent inflation due to the Iran war could have eroded that.

On Friday, the PM said he would give all mayors of city regions in England a share of income tax revenue for the first time, as part of his efforts to move power away from Westminster.

Reeves had previously said that regional mayors could be given control of some tax revenue to spend on their local priorities.

Labour pledged to devolve more powers to local councils and mayors in areas such as housing and transport as part of its 2024 election manifesto.

More details of Burnham's plan are expected to be announced in the Budget, but the government said the rate of income tax will not change as a direct result of the reforms.

AJ Bell public policy director Tom Selby said Healey "doesn't have the luxury of pointing the finger of blame at the last administration".

"Healey will likely spend a chunk of his time leafing through the thesaurus looking for new ways to rephrase the 'tough choices' message of his predecessor," he said.

Shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride said the announcement of the budget date meant "89 more days of unfunded spending commitments and damaging tax speculation until we get some details".

"Eighty-nine more days for Brits to wait before they know how much their taxes are going to go up to fund Burnham's spending addiction," he said.

News.title: Soap star Shane Richie facing drink-drive charge
News.content:
EastEnders actor Shane Richie is to appear in court charged with drink-driving, police have said.

Essex Police confirmed it was called to reports of a suspected drink-driver in the Church Langley Way area of Harlow, shortly before 23:20 BST on Wednesday.

A force spokesman confirmed the 62-year-old, of Tadworth, Surrey, was arrested and a charge of drink-driving had been authorised against him.

It added Richie, real name Shane Roche, was due to appear at Colchester Magistrates' Court on 9 September.

Richie plays Alfie Moon in EastEnders, making his first appearance in the BBC soap in 2002.

The Sun reported he was arrested, external at a Tesco petrol station forecourt.

Essex Police said: "Officers were called to reports of a suspected drink-driver in the area of Church Langley Way, Harlow, shortly before 23:20 on Wednesday, 29 July.

"On arrival, officers arrested a man.

"A charge of drink-driving has subsequently been authorised against Shane Roche, 62, of Tadworth, Surrey."

Richie's representative has been contacted for comment.
