News.title: Greek police fast-tracking tests to find out how British woman found in suitcase died
News.content:
Police investigating the death of a Scottish woman whose body was found in a suitcase in Greece say they could determine how she died "in the coming days" as they are fast-tracking toxicology tests.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was found in an abandoned building in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, reportedly by a homeless man.

The 38-year-old, known to her family as Lisa, is thought to have travelled to Greece from Edinburgh in late June, and went missing on 15 July.

Greek authorities are also looking to trace Lisa's American friends, who they said were also staying in Kypseli.

News.title: Police arrest men over alleged modern day slavery
News.content:
Two men have been arrested on suspicion of modern day slavery and money laundering offences.

Dorset Police said the 20-year-old from Sussex and a 22-year-old from Buckinghamshire were arrested during an investigation into suspected exploitation, immigration and financial offences.

Officers made the arrests after raiding a business premises in Gillingham, Dorset, it added.

Three further men were also arrested for immigration offences, the force continued.

Dorset Police said the raid followed intelligence from the community and detailed enquiries.

The force added that the "day of action" had led to a number of individuals being safeguarded.

News.title: Commonwealth Games boxing official suspended over headbutt probe
News.content:
A boxing official has been banned from serving at the Commonwealth Games over allegations he headbutted a teenage fighter in the ring.

Jon-Paul Hynd also faces claims he struck another child with an unknown object during a training session at Beath Boxing Club in Cowdenbeath, Fife.

Hynd was appointed as a technical official for the games in Glasgow, but Boxing Scotland said he had been suspended pending an investigation.

Beath Boxing Club did not respond when asked for comment by BBC Scotland News.

Complaints lodged with the sport's governing body detail claims Hynd "physically assaulted" one boxer, aged 15, by "striking him with his head" after the fighter responded to "verbal belittlement" last year.

Police Scotland investigated the incident but found no evidence of criminality.

News.title: CPS to target assets of jailed funeral director
News.content:
A disgraced funeral director's bank accounts and assets have been frozen, as prosecutors seek to recover cash fleeced from his victims.

Robert Bush was jailed for 20 years at Hull Crown Court on Friday for 67 offences, including denying 30 people a decent and proper burial and giving families the ashes of strangers.

Bush, 48, who ran Legacy Independent Funeral Directors in Hull, stole up to Â£12,000 from charities and sold fake funeral plans.

Laura Tams KC, deputy chief crown prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), said: "We will be looking at him, at the financial aspects of this case, to see if we can confiscate any of the proceeds of his crimes and try to compensate the families."

Sentencing Bush following a five-day hearing, Mr Justice Hilliard said it was clear that he "benefited very substantially" and "obviously lived very well".

Speaking exclusively to the BBC, Tams said it "was not a case of somebody that had recently fallen on hard times".

She added: "I think the scale of the offending, the length of time it had gone on for, showed that really this had become something of his business model."

News.title: Victims of disgraced funeral boss demand industry regulation
News.content:
Tristan Essex is standing on the steps of Hull Crown Court, shoulder to shoulder with several others whose lives have been devastated by disgraced funeral director Robert Bush.

The 27-year-old is fighting alongside his sister Claire for regulation of the funeral industry, a journey that has seen them take their campaign to Downing Street and resulted in a new pledge from the government "to take urgent action to crack down on rogue funeral operators".

Their grandmother Jessie Stockdale was one of Bush's victims â her body one of the 35 found at Legacy Independent Funeral Directors, five months after her funeral was held.

The news knocked the family off its feet, Tristan said. Even worse, they learned the ashes they had been given were not Jessie's remains.

This story contains details some might find distressing.

MPs are drinking so much in Parliament they are having their stomachs pumped, with alcohol “deeply embedded” in Westminster culture, a report has warned.

Alcohol is freely available all day within Westminster and drinking a commonplace pastime, according to the Institute of Alcohol Studies.

Authors warned the drinking culture is causing “real, measurable harm, and no clear route to address it” after surveying 190 MPs about the issue.

In the survey of 190 MPs and their staff, nearly 10 per cent of respondents described a negative experience due to someone else’s drinking at work. The most common were unwanted sexual attention and harassment, insults or humiliation.

Younger staff face additional risks due to “ingrained power dynamics and increased peer pressure to drink alcohol”, the report added.

It comes amid rising concerns over drinking in Westminster and a string of incidents that included a parliamentary researcher allegedly having her drink spiked at Parliament’s infamous Strangers’ Bar.

open image in gallery Parliament’s Strangers’ Bar is a favoured haunt of MPs and parliamentary staff ( PA Wire )

Green Party MP for Gorton and Denton, Hannah Spencer, criticised Westminster’s drinking culture in April this year, calling it “unprofessional and worrying,” accusing some MPs of drinking before voting.

Dr Beccy Cooper, MP for Worthing West, said: “This report is a wake-up call, but also an opportunity. Westminster is changing for the better, and this is our chance to make sure our own workplace lives up to the standards we ask of everyone else. A modern Parliament should be one that support the health and wellbeing of everyone who works here.”

The survey found:

42 per cent of MPs and 29 per cent of Westminster-based staff said they were offered alcohol at a work meeting or event on a weekly basis

Almost six in ten respondents said alcohol was more available in Westminster than in other workplaces they had experienced.

Interviewees described being handed wine at breakfast events and, at times, struggling to find a soft drink without leaving the room. One staff member said: “No other workplace I’ve had produces its own wine.

The report described the easy accessibility of alcohol on the Parliament estate.

“The availability of alcohol was seen to encourage unhealthy behaviour in general, from affecting colleagues’ sleep and stress levels to potentially normalising high-risk drinking, with one MP referring to colleagues having had their stomachs pumped in hospital and going back into Westminster the following day,” it said.

“A staff member warned of the temporary sense of relaxation alcohol provided from the daily stresses of the job without addressing the underlying issues.”

open image in gallery Green Party MP Hannah Spencer tried to raise the issue of Westminster drinking in Parliament ( PA )

When asked about how to improve the situation, most survey participants said they accepted that alcohol would be present in parliament, such as in on-site bars, but did not have to be freely available at all hours.

Dr Katherine Severi, Chief Executive of the Institute of Alcohol Studies, said: “Parliament has modernised in many ways over recent years, but our findings suggest there is still work to do to ensure it is a healthy, safe and inclusive place to work.

“MPs and staff interviewed for this study made constructive, common-sense recommendations, such as limiting the provision of free alcohol to evening events and improving support and signposting for people experiencing alcohol problems while working in Parliament.”

“This is also a policy issue. If alcohol remains unusually central to the working culture of Parliament, there is a risk that the scale of alcohol harm across the UK is not seen as clearly as it should be.

“A healthier parliamentary workplace would support the people who work there and help create the conditions for more serious, evidence-based action on alcohol harm.”

Massive Attack has been banned from entering Singapore after holding up a Palestinian flag at one of their shows in the Southeast Asian country.

The British band, best known for hits like “Unfinished Sympathy” and “Teardrop”, performed at Singapore’s Star Theatre on Wednesday (29 July), with two members shouting “free Palestine” and holding up the Palestinian flag during the gig.

In Singapore, it is illegal to display all foreign flags and national emblems without a permit due to the country’s strict public speech and assembly laws.

Singapore’s police force announced on Friday (31 July) that the two band members were given “stern warnings” and “will also be banned from re-entering Singapore”.

open image in gallery Massive Attack band members hold up a Palestinian flag during their Singapore concert ( Reuters )

Meanwhile, the country’s media regulator – the Infocomm Media Development Authority – said that it “will also not grant any future application for performances by the band in Singapore in view of the entry ban”.

In a joint statement, the police and IMDA continued: “The Police take a serious view of acts which could potentially harm the racial and religious harmony in Singapore and urge the public, including foreigners, to refrain from importing foreign politics as this can undermine our social cohesion and the rule of law.

“The peace and harmony between different races and religions in Singapore should not be taken for granted, and we must not let external events affect our society.”

The Independent has contacted Massive Attack’s representatives for comment.

The band, which was formed in Bristol in 1988, currently consists of Robert “3D” Del Naja and Grant “Daddy G” Marshall – with former members Andrew Vowles and Adrian Thaws having left in 1999 and 2016 respectively.

Over the years, they have won a number of awards, including a Brit Award for Best British Dance Act in 1996 and an Ivor Novello for Outstanding Contribution to British Music in 2009.

open image in gallery Grant Marshall of Massive Attack ( Getty Images )

The members of Massive Attack are vocal opponents of Israel’s military actions in Gaza; in April, frontman Robert Del Naja was arrested on suspicion of showing support for a proscribed organisation after attending a mass protest against the ban on Palestine Action in central London.

Just a week later, the band signed an open letter which called for Eurovision fans to boycott the 2026 contest over Israel’s participation. The letter, which was organised by No Music for Genocide and the BDS movement, called for the European Broadcasting Union to ban Israel’s public broadcaster, KAN, from the contest – however, the country was still allowed to take part when the competition took place in May.

Earlier this year, Massive Attack released its first track in over a decade: protest song “Boots on the Ground”. A collaboration with Tom Waits, the song was accompanied by a music video featuring visuals of anti-ICE demonstrations in America as well as Black Lives Matter protests, which were sparked by the murder of George Floyd in Minneapolis in 2020.

The band is currently on an international tour, with performances scheduled this month in South Korea and Australia.

News.content:

For Palestinians in Gaza, President Donald Trump's announcement that Hamas had agreed to disarm was a small sign of hope that Israel's attacks might end, allowing them to rebuild their lives and what remains of their homes.

But it also clashed with the reality on the ground, where Israeli strikes have continued since Trump first touted the deal late Thursday in Washington, and where few steps have been taken to advance a broader ceasefire agreement that went into effect in October.

Most of Gaza’s 2 million Palestinians are still displaced or live in tent camps, where poor conditions and overcrowding have led to rodent infestations and outbreaks of infectious diseases such as chickenpox.

“They can talk about withdrawal and disarmament," said Abdel Moneim Aboul-Roos, 24, a tuk-tuk driver who lost his leg in an Israeli airstrike. “I don’t care about any of it as long as there is no food or medicine.”

Israel and Hamas signed a U.S.-backed ceasefire plan last year that ended major combat operations, saw the return of Israeli hostages and allowed for an increase in humanitarian aid to the Palestinian enclave. It also called for the gradual withdrawal of Israeli troops, the creation of an international stabilization force and a program to decommission weapons held by Hamas.

But as each side accused the other of violating the ceasefire, negotiations stalled. Hamas held onto its weapons and the Israeli military refused to withdraw. Since October, Israel has killed more than 1,200 Palestinians in Gaza and expanded the amount of territory it controls. Five Israeli soldiers have also been killed in militant attacks.

Many Palestinians don't trust Israel or Hamas

The road map Trump announced — and that Hamas confirmed — addresses in more specific terms the type of weapons the militant group and its allies will be required to hand over to a new technocratic government. The document says Israel will not be involved in the decommission of Hamas' weapons and that it should halt all military operations in Gaza so the transition can proceed and recovery can begin.

But residents in Gaza say they have been repeatedly promised that the war will stop and their lives will improve. They see the road map as a positive development but remain skeptical that either Israel or Hamas will adhere to the terms.

“This is enough. We need improvement in our lives,” said Ayman Ahmed, a displaced Palestinian living in southern Gaza. He said he hopes Hamas gives up its arms but does not see it happening anytime soon.

“They don't care about Palestinians’ lives,” he said.

The war began when Hamas-led militants attacked southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, killing around 1,200 people and taking 251 others back to Gaza as hostages. Israel's retaliatory offensive has killed more than 73,300 people, according to the Gaza Health Ministry, which was part of the Hamas-run government.

The ministry maintains detailed records viewed as generally reliable by U.N. agencies and international organizations. It does not distinguish between civilians and militants, but says women and children make up around half of all fatalities.

Because of the high death toll and ongoing attacks, other Palestinians say they believe Israel will refuse to make concessions.

In southern Gaza, Ghazal Astal lives among the rubble. She said there is near-constant Israeli gunfire and that the territory has been transformed into an “indescribable battlefield.”

Ammar Kaskeen, 30, said he doesn't believe the road map will force Israeli troops to withdraw. For Israel, according to Kaskeen, the goal is not only to disarm Hamas but to also drive the Palestinian population out of Gaza.

"They will make us suffer,” he said.

Even as Israel digs in, Palestinians dream of returning home

Israel has not commented publicly on the road map but Israeli officials, speaking anonymously over the past two days, have signaled that the document does not align with the country's interests.

The officials also reiterated that Israel would not withdraw from the Yellow Line in Gaza, which divides Israeli-controlled territory in the east with the western part of the enclave.

In recent months, the military has built a massive earthen barrier roughly along the same line, developing what it described as a “security zone” adjacent to the berm, equipped with intelligence and technological assets.

Israel has also carried out controlled demolitions and clearing operations across much of the territory it controls. Palestinians who lived there have yet to return — and are unsure whether their homes are still standing.

Anas Nakla was displaced from Rafah in southern Gaza during the war. He said he knows his house has been destroyed but still wants to return home with his wife and children.

“It doesn't exist anymore," he said. "But we can return and rebuild.”

Similarly, Mohamed Hamad, who had to leave his home behind in northern Gaza, hopes that the U.S.-backed road map will pressure Israel to leave some of the areas it controls. He believes that even if only a small number of people could go back to their homes, “it will give hope to the rest that some day they may also return.”

___

Melanie Lidman and Sam Mednick contributed to this report from Tel Aviv, Israel.

Authorities ended a massive dayslong search-and-rescue operation Saturday at a collapsed shopping mall in southwest Japan following a powerful earthquake that killed 34 people earlier this week.

The magnitude 7.1 earthquake hit Kumamoto Prefecture on Japan’s southern main island of Kyushu on Tuesday. The Aeon Mall, in the town of Kashima, was one of the hardest-hit sites, after an explosion that followed the quake caused the walls and a floor to collapse.

The explosion, which the company said it believes was due to a gas leak, occurred after about 3,000 shoppers had been evacuated to a parking lot following the quake, but some employees remained inside. The mall’s second floor collapsed.

Rescuers extracted five people from under mall debris and retrieved the bodies of seven others over the past five days. On Saturday, officials said all the missing were accounted for and ended the operation at the mall.

The overall number of missing in the hit prefecture remains unknown, and search operations pressed on, with thousands of Self Defense troops, police, rescue workers and sniffing dogs deployed.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, at a government task force meeting Saturday, urged rescue personnel not to leave anyone behind.

At another hard-hit site in Kumamoto Prefecture, a chimney collapsed at the Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro city, trapping 11 employees. Nine have since been confirmed dead and two were rescued, officials said.

The earthquake has left 103 people injured in Kumamoto, authorities said, and two in addition to the reported deaths are being investigated to determine if they are quake-related.

The prefecture’s main challenge is the lack of fresh water affecting nearly 70,000 homes, and fuel shortages as Japan suffers sweltering heat, stoking fears of heat-related illness. Japan Meteorological Agency said temperatures reached an “extreme heat” level of 36.6 degrees Celsius (97.8 degrees Fahrenheit) in Kumamoto city Saturday.

More than 9,000 people remain at crowded shelters, such as converted community centers, school gyms and classrooms. Many others slept in cars parked at town hall parking lots and parks, or outside of their homes, for privacy.

Experts have long criticized Japan’s crowded conditions at emergency shelters, arguing that a lack of sanitation and privacy creates additional stress and increases the risk of health problems for disaster-hit people.

Water, food and other necessities, including portable toilets, as well as air conditioners and partitions, were being delivered to improve conditions at the evacuation centers, Takaichi said Saturday.

“The government is determined to do everything we can,” Takaichi said.

The prefecture said it has received more than 1,500 reports of power loss as of Saturday, but local power company serving Kyushu said it had no immediate reports of outages.

Over 180 homes were destroyed, officials said, and nearly 3,500 buildings were damaged — nearly double the number reported on Friday — with 20 of them severely affected, according to Kumamoto prefectural assessments.

EastEnders’ Shane Richie has been charged with a drink-driving offence after being arrested at an Essex petrol station.

The actor, 62, was filmed arguing with staff at a Tesco garage on Wednesday (29 July) after being asked to stop vaping on the petrol station forecourt.

The police were subsequently called, with the EastEnders star – whose real name is Shane Roche – being arrested for drink-driving. A spokesperson for the Essex Police told The Independent: “Officers were called to reports of a suspected drink driver in the area of Church Langley Way, Harlow, shortly before 11.20pm on Wednesday 29 July.

“On arrival, officers arrested a man. A charge of drink driving has subsequently been authorised against Shane Roche, 62, of Tadworth, Surrey. He is due to appear at Colchester Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday 9 September.”

Shane Richie on ‘EastEnders’ with Jessie Wallace

In footage obtained by The Sun, the Alfie Moon actor was seen holding a vape by his car and telling staff: “It’s not smoking, it’s a vape.” After being asked not to use his e-cigarette by the staff, he is heard telling them to “f*** off”.

“I don’t give a f***,” he added, before later telling them: “Someone is coming to change my tyre.”

The Independent has contacted Richie’s representative for comment.

The comedian and actor is best known for playing Alfie Moon on BBC soap EastEnders, having first joined in 2002. In recent years, he’s appeared on Michael McIntyre’s Big Show, Benidorm and I’m a Celebrity, Get Me Out of Here – coming in fourth place in the 2020 series.

Last year saw Richie become the focus of a big storyline in Albert Square, with Alfie marrying Kat Slater (Jessie Wallace) for the third time. The well-known Walford couple had previously wed in 2003 and again in 2014 despite multiple infidelities.

Richie was previously married to Loose Women star Coleen Nolan from 1990 until 1999, with the pair sharing sons Shane Jr, 38, and Rixton frontman Jake Roche, 33.

He went on to remarry in 2007, tying the knot with actor Christie Goddard. The couple welcomed three daughters: Mackenzie Blue, 20, Lolita Bell, 18, and Romanie-Skye, 15.

WNBA star Brittney Griner has filed for divorce from wife Cherelle Griner, and is seeking joint physical custody of their two-year-old son.

The Connecticut Sun center, 35, has been married to Cherelle, who heavily advocated for the basketball player’s release from a Russian prison in 2022, for eight years.

On Thursday, Brittney submitted a petition to the Superior Court of Fulton County, Georgia, for the dissolution of marriage. The filing, obtained by ABC News, stated that the couple has been separated since July 24, 2026, and that the marriage “is irretrievably broken” with “no hope of reconciliation.”

Brittney has requested joint physical custody of their son, Bash, whom they welcomed in 2024, as well as “equitable division” of all marital debts and assets, “both real and personal, tangible and intangible.”

An attorney representing Brittney told the outlet in a statement, “This is a matter we hope the parties can resolve privately. There is no further comment at this time.”

open image in gallery Brittney Griner married second wife Cherelle in 2019 ( Getty Images )

The Independent has contacted Brittney and Cherelle’s representatives for comment.

Brittney’s divorce filing comes four years after she was freed from Russia in a prisoner swap. The athlete had originally been detained at a Moscow airport in February 2022 after vape cartridges containing cannabis oil — a drug strictly illegal in Russia — were found in her luggage.

She pleaded guilty to drug-possession charges and was sentenced to nine years in a penal colony.

Cherelle led a months-long campaign, working closely with the Biden administration to advocate for Brittney’s release.

“I won’t go down until she’s back ... every single day matters for me to be sound, for me to be alert, for me to be attentive, to make sure that she comes back,” Cherelle, who is a lawyer, said on a May 2022 segment of Good Morning America.

open image in gallery WNBA star is seeking joint custody of their two-year-old son, Bash ( Getty Images )

Brittney ultimately spent 10 months in Russian detention before she was released in a prisoner swap in December 2022.

In her first interview following her release, Brittney revealed that she “wanted to take my life more than once in the first weeks.”

“I felt like leaving here so badly,” she told ABC’s Robin Roberts in 2024. “I could just visualize everything I worked so hard for just crumbling and going away.”

The WNBA veteran was previously married to retired WNBA player Glory Johnson, with whom she shares twins, Ava Simone and Solei Diem. The pair got divorced a year after tying the knot in 2015.

“Today” show host Savannah Guthrie on Saturday said on social media that her family was “desperate” and “begging for help” in the disappearance of her mother, a day after authorities released two ransom notes including one saying that she had died.

Authorities released an early note in the investigation into the disappearance of 84-year-old Nancy Guthrie, hoping that someone will recognize the writing style. A second note said Guthrie died shortly after she was kidnapped and “is buried in nature now.” Both notes initially were sent to a Tucson television station days after Guthrie went missing from her home outside Tucson on Feb. 1.

“We are begging for help. We are desperate. We need someone to come forward. Someone knows something. Someone suspects something. Someone recognizes the writing in the ransom demand notes,” Guthrie wrote on her Instagram account, alongside a photo of her mother.

“Someone has noticed something different, strange, troubling or just unusual - perhaps with someone they deeply love," she wrote. "Perhaps they are afraid to come forward. Perhaps they are conflicted. Perhaps they are angry or upset for being in this situation. There is a way out - to tell what you know.”

Guthrie went on to say they “wanted to find out what happened to her, so that we can give her the dignity of a proper goodbye - a celebration of her remarkable life that she so deserves.”

Saturday is the six-month mark since Guthrie disappeared. No suspects have been arrested. The investigation has been dogged by unanswered questions, such as how many people are believed to have taken part in her abduction and whether she was taken by someone who knew her.

The FBI in Washington did not respond to questions about the ransom notes, including whether both messages sent to the Tucson station have been deemed legitimate.

In releasing the notes, the Pima County Sheriff’s Department said “we believe these distinctive linguistic characteristics may be recognizable to someone who knows or has interacted with the notes’ writer.”

The first note, sent Feb. 2, said Guthrie was safe but scared and would be released unharmed once her captors received $4 million in cryptocurrency, with the ransom amount increasing if the first demand was not met. It said Guthrie would be released within 12 hours if the payment was received. It also included a threat to kill her if the ransom wasn’t paid.

“Your mother is aware of this and her life is in your hands,” the first note read. “It is in the best interest of everyone to have this completed as soon as possible.”

The second note was sent Feb. 6 and said Guthrie died shortly after she was taken. “She is buried in nature now,” it said. “Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome.” The note ended with an apology: “We are truly sorry.”

The sheriff’s department said the notes reveal a distinctive pattern of word choices and provide insight into the writer’s mindset. The agency said someone who knows the notes’ writer may recognize the patterns.

Authorities similarly used a suspect’s own writings as a tool to apprehend Theodore “Ted” Kaczynski, branded the “Unabomber” by the FBI. Kaczynski, who killed three people and injured 23 others with mail bombs over a 17-year span, pressured The Washington Post, in conjunction with The New York Times, to publish his 35,000-word manifesto in 1995.

The sheriff’s office also said Friday that two videos recovered from Guthrie’s doorbell camera might be from two separate days and indicate an unidentified male prepared ahead of when Guthrie was taken. Authorities are seeking information on anyone who was behaving differently, changed their physical appearance, suddenly left the Tucson area, or had a noticeable or unexplained interest or disinterest in the case.

“Investigators continue to pursue every available technological and investigative lead,” the sheriff’s office said. “However, community members remain a vital resource as we seek to provide answers for Nancy’s family.”

The FBI had released surveillance videos of a masked person who authorities said appeared to tamper with a camera on Nancy Guthrie’s front porch and block it with a plant. They described the person as a male about 5 feet, 9 inches (1.75 meters) tall.

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery friendly with Chelsea
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.



Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

News.title: Battle rages over access to new ‘miracle’ HIV drug
News.content:
For the first time in the four-decade fight against HIV there is a “miracle” drug that can all but eliminate the risk of infection, but in the Latin American countries where it was tested almost no one can get it.

Trials show that Lenacapavir, made by Gilead Sciences, is almost 100 per cent effective in preventing HIV infection. With just two shots a year, those taking it will avoid contracting the virus even when frequently exposed.

The drug, which many believe could bring an end to the global HIV pandemic, costs $14,000 a dose in the United States. Gilead has agreed to licence generic versions of the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) medication at around $40 a dose in 120 low-and middle-income countries, but almost all of Latin America is excluded.

Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Peru are among those with serious HIV epidemics that are shut out, despite having run some of the clinical trials that proved the drug works.

Their status as “upper-middle income countries” means they are too rich to qualify for the cut price generic version and yet they remain too poor to pay the US price.

News.title: Senior dating: a guide to finding love later in life
News.content:
Whether you’re a widow, widower or divorcee, the thought of online dating in later life can feel daunting. However, more and more people are turning to the internet to find romance. Roughly 16 per cent of UK adults are using online dating services to meet a partner, according to Statista. Among them, there are lots of singles over 50 using dating sites.

So here’s how to navigate your senior dating online, with expert advice from psychologist and dating coach Dr Pam Spurr, and sex and relationship coach Angela Vossen.

How do I know if I'm ready to date again as a senior?

Coming out of any relationship is hard. If you’re hoping to date after a divorce, bereavement or break up, it can take a long time to feel ready to date again. Dr Spurr advises taking your time.

“Many people feel bruised, even traumatised, after coming out of a long-term relationship or having been bereaved,” she explains. “Your feelings naturally vary from day to day about whether you're ready to get back out to look for love – or even for fun. A crucial factor is if you've come to the point where you have more good days compared to bad days”.

Dr Spurr explains that good days are the days on which you feel more optimistic about life generally, and you find your thoughts turning to meeting someone new. “That's an important sign that you are healing,” she says. “However, if you're still feeling deeply insecure or are riddled with self-doubt about your worthiness, take your time. When you feel worthy, you will find someone worthy of you”.

Feeling heartbroken? Learn how to get over a break up

How to start senior dating online

If you’re new to online dating, it can feel intimidating at first. The secret is taking things step by step so that you do things at your own pace. The first step, however, should be choosing a senior dating site that will help match you with like-minded people. This will narrow your search and ensure your dating experience is more successful.

Step 1: Create an online profile

Once you’ve decided on a dating site or app and signed up, you’ll be asked to write a dating profile. This should reflect who you are along with your passions, values and what you seek in a partner.

Try to be authentic rather than creating a fantasy version of yourself. If you exaggerate your accomplishments, your date will only feel deceived once they get to know you. Likewise, don’t be tempted to use a photo of yourself from 10 years ago.

What are you waiting for? |  Single and looking to find true love? Sign up today for Telegraph Dating and join more than 220,000 like-minded people. Join today

Step 2: Spark meaningful chats with potential dates

Once you have signed up to a senior dating site and created a profile, you will be free to start looking at other people’s profiles and sending messages to anyone that catches your attention. But how can you initiate a conversation after an introduction?

“When messaging people on dating sites, ask open-ended questions to spark meaningful chats,” says Angela. A good example would be, ‘I can see you enjoy travel. What place have you always wanted to visit but haven’t yet?’ or “tell me more about your love of tennis? Did you watch the US Open?” If things go really well and the chat seems to flow naturally, you may decide to organise a phone chat or ask them out on a date. An initial chat over the phone can help gauge how well you get on and how easily the conversation flows. If this goes well, meeting in person may feel less nerve wracking and a little less ‘blind’.

Step 3: Prioritise your safety

“While most people are well intentioned online, it’s important to protect your safety,” advises Ms Vossen. “Keep personal details private (like where you live or your social media profiles) until you’ve met in person and built trust”. You should also arrange first dates in public places, share your plans with a friend, and trust your instincts if something feels off.

If the first date or two doesn’t quite hit the mark, try not to be too disappointed and remember that you can say no to another date. Ms Vossen says: “Be patient – online dating takes time, but with practice, you’ll gain confidence and enjoy the journey”.

Traditional ways to meet senior singles

Of course, couples continue to meet in a manner that predates online dating sites. If you’re keen to join the older dating scene but find the online world overwhelming, there are plenty of ways to meet people in real life.

1. Holidays and group trips

We are often our best selves on holiday, so it’s the ideal place to find a single senior woman or to meet men if the opportunity presents itself. Why not organise a trip on which you meet new people while doing what you love, whether that’s cycling, walking, sightseeing or just travelling around a new part of the world. There are many escorted tours that cater to specific age groups and interests. They also take away the stress of organising a trip yourself.

“An organised holiday or trip can be a great place to meet someone new and there are many organisations offering these for the over 50s,” says Dr Spur. “A word of caution though, you can spend a lot of money and there's no guarantee that you will meet that special person. However, if it's a place you've wanted to travel to then go with the mindset that you're going to have a great trip. If you meet someone, that's an added bonus”.

2. Activities and social groups

Whether you enjoy walking, reading or volunteering, taking up a new hobby or joining a social group is a great way to enhance your social life and increase your chances of meeting a new romantic interest.

“Joining a club or taking up a hobby can be a fantastic way of meeting singles who enjoy the same pastimes,” says Dr Spur. “You're doing an activity you enjoy knowing that there might also be someone there that will catch your eye”.

If you do meet someone that you’re interested in at a social event, Dr Spur advises starting with a simple ‘hello’ and an easy question such as how long they've been doing that particular activity or hobby. “This can open-up a friendly conversation that might lead to flirting down the line,” she says.

Start online dating for seniors today

Whichever way you decide to start looking for love, approach it in a way that you feel comfortable with. Signing up to an online dating service is a great way to meet other seniors. Remember, it’s never too late to begin a new chapter.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

Sports.title: FA demands ‘full and robust review of Fifa’ in scathing statement after Gianni Infantino’s failed plot to sell World Cup
Sports.content:
GIANNI INFANTINO and Fifa have come under fire again as The FA slam his controversial World Cup plot and demand a review.

The Fifa president announced a u-turn on the plans to transfer control of top tournaments like the World Cup to a new subsidiary, followed by the sale of a substantial portion of the business.



The FA had previously blasted the proposals as they alerted everyone to lack of details and answers provided.

On August 1, the FA spokesperson said: “We fully support UEFA’s position.



“It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long – term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Initially, the world’s governing football body planned to sell minority, non-controlling shares in FFE, with the aims of raising £3.1billion – which the organisation valued at around £15bn.

And in a majorly bold mistep, Infantino offered £30million to each of the nations that got on side.

UEFA were quick to condemn the plans as they pointed to “governance by intimidation”.

Federations everywhere stepped up to call Infantino and Fifa out, with many stating plans to boycott tournaments.

Even Infantino’s senior advisor Carlos Codeiro resigned, calling the whole thing a “bad deal for the game”.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Since then UEFA has publicly announced that they have lost confidence in Infantino’s Fifa reign.

They have also accused Infantino of not delivering on promises as they quoted a speech he gave when campaigning to become Fifa president in 2016.

The whole debacle has piled pressure on Infantino before he seeks re-election for a fourth term as president at the Fifa Congress in March.

Sports.title: Bayern Munich ‘want Man Utd star Benjamin Sesko in shock transfer with Harry Kane lined up for shock new position’
Sports.content:
BAYERN MUNICH are interested in buying Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – and they are prepared to play Harry Kane somewhere else.

The German giants are reportedly exploring a move for Sesko, 23, after his impressive first year in England .



He scored 12 times in all competitions from 32 games – ending with a streak of nine in 14 after Ruben Amorim was sacked.

Sesko was a target for Bayern in 2024 before signing a new contract at RB Leipzig, and then Vincent Kompany‘s side could not afford him.



But they are prepared to go big on Sesko if the chance arises, Christian Falk told CFBayern Insider.

He suggests that with star No9 Kane dropping deeper as he gets older, space may well open up in the frontline.

Last season Bayern had Nicolas Jackson on loan from Chelsea as a backup but he barely got a sniff in meaningful matches as Kane remained fit.

Now they have signed Morocco World Cup ace Ismael Saibari from PSV Eindhoven and are preparing a new deal for Kane.

But Falk says Bayern could be tempted to go for Sesko in the future.

It is claimed that should the Slovenian struggle in his second year in the Prem, Bayern would offer him a way out.

Sports.title: Man City preparing shock bid for Pedro Neto with Chelsea keen to negotiate transfer for around £70MILLION
Sports.content:
MAN CITY are lining up a shock bid for £70million-rated Chelsea star Pedro Neto.

The 26-year-old has been linked with a move away from Stamford Bridge this summer.



A move to City would reunite him with ex-Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca, who has just taken over from old mentor Pep Guardiola.

City have already snapped up Nottingham Forest star Elliot Anderson for a British transfer record of £116m.



Jeremy Monga has also arrived from Leicester, but now Maresca wants to be reunited with his old Chelsea star Neto.

City have officially entered the race to sign the Portugal international amid competition from AC Milan.

Milan have placed Neto at the top of their wishlist and see him as a potental replacement for Rafael Leao amid doubts over his future.

But any deal for Neto hinges on Leao’s exit as the Serie A giants are hoping to use the funds towards the move.

Neto moving to City is also a possibility as Maresca sees him as an ideal fit for his system.

SunSport understands City chiefs are exploring a deal after the Italian voiced his desire to work with the player again.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, Chelsea have slapped a £70m price-tag on Neto and are in no rush to sell him.

The club consider the winger an important member of their squad but accept that a big offer could change their position.

Chelsea could be forced to do business to balance the books after laying out £117m to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Europe is not the only option for Neto, with his agent Jorge Mendes also offering him to Saudi club Al-Hilal.



But the Middle East isn’t a realistic destination for the player as the club are prioritising other areas of their squad.

Not to mention Neto isn’t keen on a move to Saudi at this point in his career and wants to remain at the top level.

The former Wolves man has been informed of the interest from both AC Milan and Man City and he is open to both proposals.

The player – who made 30 starts for the Blues last season – is happy to wait it out and see what happens towards the end of the window.

Sports.title: Chelsea 1 Tottenham 2: Richarlison snatches last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs as Alonso faces Blues formation conundrum
Sports.content:
THERE was no love lost between Chelsea and Tottenham – THOUSANDS of miles away from London.

The two teams played out a competitive friendly in Sydney as a summer tour turned sour – with Spurs coming out on top in stoppage time.



Roberto De Zerbi‘s men had Kevin Danso sent off just three minutes into the second half after bringing down Joao Pedro, changing the dynamic of the game.

He looked furious on the bench and sat down contemplating what it meant for his preparations.



Danso missed his first touch and hauled down the Chelsea man when through on goal.

It was a certain red in competitive matches but there will be questions over if it was entirely necessary here.



Tottenham had gone ahead early on through Sandro Tonali‘s deflected strike in front of more than 80,000 at the Accor Stadium.

Chelsea responded well and hit back via Estevao Willian‘s back post header.

Spurs had the better of things before the break but Mathys Tel was denied by Blues backup Teddy Sharman-Lowe.

Chelsea thought they had scored to move ahead just after Danso’s red but Antonin Kinsky somehow tipped Estevao’s close range effort onto the bar – even though it came off his own player first.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Kinsky came to the rescue again when Andy Robertson let Joao Pedro have an effort inside his own six yard box.

On a shocking pitch – which has now had six games played on it since last weekend – both managers opted for more subs than risk pushing for a win.



Spurs came close to finding a late victory before penalties when youngster Rio Kyerematen struck the bar from distance after a surging run.

They then found a dagger through Richarlison to take the bragging rights back to England.

The Brazilian tapped in after a rebound with Jamie Donley’s dribbling effort coming off the post.

It left De Zerbi with a trophy to lift and some confidence gained, especially from Tel, who impressed again.

Sports.title: Spurs star Kevin Danso shown straight red in friendly vs Chelsea after horror gaffe just three minutes after coming on
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM defender Kevin Danso was sent off just minutes after coming on in a pre-season friendly against Chelsea.

Roberto De Zerbi‘s men had only just kicked off the second half in Sydney and were drawing 1-1 after Sandro Tonali‘s strike was cancelled out by Estevao.



But Danso gave Spurs an uphill task against Chelsea after slipping and dragging down Joao Pedro as the last man.

The 27-year-old was shown a straight red card and the Austria international headed down the tunnel.



Danso was so often a reliable figure for De Zerbi during Tottenham‘s Premier League survival campaign last season.

Spurs fans cursed their luck and slammed Danso for his lapse in concentration.



One said on X: “Why do you do this in a friendly match?! Danso should have just let him go.”

A second added: “Wtf are you doing Danso?”

A third wrote: “Just let him go, there’s enough time to equalise. Silly tackle from Danso to cost the whole team.”

And another commented: “Why’s he doing that in a friendly? So what if Chelsea scores, the match means nothing.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But others insisted it was a harsh decision given it was a friendly and both teams simply needed match fitness.

One added: “So irritating and stupid of the ref to send off Danso there to be honest – just have a word, tell him to calm down and get on with it. Pathetic.”

Danso has just returned from playing at the World Cup with Austria, where he featured four times.

He played a total of 239 minutes, starting their Round of 32 clash against eventual winner Spain, which they lost 3-0.



Danso played 35 games for Tottenham last season as he helped rescue them from the drop.

But his minutes look set to drop this season after Spurs signed two high profile centre-backs in Jan-Paul van Hecke from Brighton and Marcos Senesi from Bournemouth.

Sports.title: ‘The team miss him and I will miss him’ – Barcelona boss Hansi Flick hints he DID want to sign Marcus Rashford
Sports.content:
HANSI FLICK hinted that he wanted to hold on to Manchester United loanee Marcus Rashford at the end of last season.

Rashford spent the campaign on loan with La Blaugrana following his United exile under Ruben Amorim, with the Spanish giants storming to the LaLiga title.



But despite rumours about the club looking to trigger his £26million buy-option, he ended up returning to Old Trafford.

Flick admitted he will miss the star, and suggested that the decision on his future was out of his control at the Camp Nou.



He said: “What I can say about Marcus is I appreciate a lot to work with him. Sometimes it’s not always that you do know what happens with the players who are on loan.

“I think our situation is not easy for that, but I appreciate a lot working with him as he’s a fantastic player and fantastic person. I think also the team miss him and I will miss him, but that’s life. This is what we have to accept.”

The manager did, however, praise his £70m replacement, fellow England World Cup star Anthony Gordon, who Flick says is “on fire” to get going at his new home.

The Barcelona hierarchy had the choice to fork out for Rashford’s buy-option, but apparently preferred to splash the cash on Gordon.

The former Magpies ace did not feature as Barcelona were held to a thrilling 2-2 draw by Birmingham before the Blues claimed a 3-2 penalty shootout victory in front of a sold-out St Andrew’s.

But the 25-year-old was still one of the biggest talking points after Flick revealed just how eager the England international has been since agreeing his move.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Barcelona boss said: “At the end, Anthony Gordon comes and from the first call with him when I spoke with him, he’s on fire for Barcelona and he wants to go there and I’m really happy that he is now in our team.”

Gordon arrived after three seasons at Newcastle following his switch from Everton in 2023.

The 25-year-old enjoyed a superb Champions League campaign last season for Newcastle, scoring ten goals – with only Kylian Mbappe (15) and Harry Kane (14) managing more.

One of those strikes came against Barcelona during Newcastle’s 2-1 group-stage defeat at St James’ Park before the Spanish giants eliminated the Magpies 8-3 on aggregate in the last 16 after a 1-1 draw in England and a 7-2 victory at the Camp Nou.



But he will have to wait to make his first contributions in the blue and red after missing out on a thrilling friendly against unusual opposition.

Birmingham took the lead after 31 minutes when August Priske headed home Alex Cochrane‘s inviting cross.

Barcelona levelled just before the break after they were awarded a penalty when Christoph Klarer fouled Hamza Abdelkarim, who converted before adding his second shortly after the hour when James Beadle spilled Roony Bardghji’s effort into his path.

The hosts refused to give in and Jhon Solis made it 2-2 after Klarer headed Cochrane’s free-kick back across goal.



Cochrane then came within inches of a stunning winner when his half-volley crashed against the crossbar before Beadle produced a brilliant late double save to deny Bardghji and Alex Gonzalez.

The game went to penalties, where Birmingham came out on top 3-2.

Scott Wright, Ethan Laird and Patrick Roberts converted for the Blues, while Luis Vazquez and Jack Robinson were denied by Aron Yaakobishvili.

Barcelona’s Bardghji saw his effort saved by Beadle, Jordi Pesquer hit the top of the bar, and Brian Farinas was also denied by Beadle as Birmingham secured the shootout victory.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Among those watching from the stands was Gordon’s England team-mate Jude Bellingham, who wore a Birmingham shirt while sitting alongside his parents Denise and Mark.



The pair will be El Clasico rivals next season, with Bellingham wearing the famous white for Jose Mourinho‘s Real Madrid, with Gordon on the opposite team in blue and red.

Sports.title: Watch the awkward moment England football legend gets BOOED as he downs a pint onstage during Luke Combs gig
Sports.content:
WATCH the unfortunate moment an ex-England ace gets BOOED by the crowd after taking to the stage during Luke Combs’ gig at Wembley Stadium.

The soccer star even cheekily downed a pint during his surprise stage appearance, as the country singer egged him on – but his antics didn’t appear to appease the crowd.



Ex-England defender and former Chelsea captain John Terry randomly joined Luke on-stage for the first night of his three-show run at Wembley.

The 45-year-old was seen sneaking up behind the Country music star, before the two shared a hug on-stage.



But his appearance was mostly met with boos and jeers from the crowd.

The pair then walked down centre stage together with a can of beer each and proceeded to down the contents.

Showing he still had the moves, John then booted his empty can straight into the crowd.

Luke then gave the ex-footballer a slap on the back after finishing his pint, before launching back into his song “1, 2 Many” about hitting the bottle with friends.



Meanwhile, John retreated and headed off stage to presumably enjoy the rest of the concert.

John enjoyed a hugely successful career playing for The Blues, winning 17 trophies during his 19-year reign.

The former England captain retired from football in 2018 whilst at Aston Villa.

After retiring, he joined the coaching staff at Villa Park, becoming Dean Smiths assistant coach.

He left his post at Villa in 2021 believing he would find a senior management role.



He was briefly linked to a role at Newcastle in 2021, but nothing materialised and the job went to Eddie Howe.

He had a short stint as assistant coach with Leicester City and later joined the backroom staff for Chelsea‘s academy in 2023, where he remains today.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Vinicius Jr update, Bruno Guimaraes latest and Man Utd step up move
Sports.content:
Chelsea and FA drop Mykhailo Mudryk statement

Mykhailo Mudryk will now be available to play for Chelsea. A statement from the FA confirmed the news, saying: "The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026.

"In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility. On 22 October 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance.

"The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on 4 December 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On 23 May 2025, The FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

"Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

"Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

Chelsea also uploaded their own statement which said: "Chelsea FC acknowledges today's announcement by The Football Association confirming the resolution of the anti-doping proceedings involving Mykhailo Mudryk.

"From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

"We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process. We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted.

"That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward. "Misha has consistently maintained that he never knowingly or intentionally used a prohibited substance and did not know how traces of the substance entered his system. Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

"We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career. Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations. Everyone at the Club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch."

Sports.title: Barcelona boss speaks out on Marcus Rashford as deal turned down - ‘I miss him’
Sports.content:
Barcelona boss speaks out on Marcus Rashford as deal turned down - ‘I miss him’

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United after Barcelona turned down the chance to sign him permanently following a season-long loan switch at the Nou Camp

View 2 Images Hansi Flick has discussed the decision not to sign Marcus Rashford permanently (Image: Getty Images)

Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has said that the Spanish giants ‘miss’ Marcus Rashford following his return to Manchester United. The England wideman spent last season on loan in Spain.

‌



The Catalan giants had an option to sign him permanently for £26m but turned down that opportunity. It leaves Rashford in a difficult situation.

‌



As it stands, no clubs have made an approach to United to sign him, while he is valued at £40m by the Red Devils.

‌



Barcelona boss Flick has now discussed the winger following the club’s decision not to go through with a permanent deal and certainly has a high opinion of the wideman. He said: “What I can say about Marcus is I appreciate a lot to work with him. Sometimes it’s not always that you do know what happens with the players who are on loan.

Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed READ MORE :

“I think our situation is not easy for that, but I appreciate a lot working with him as he’s a fantastic player and fantastic person. I think also the team miss him and I will miss him, but that’s life. This is what we have to accept.”

While Barcelona opted not to sign Rashford, they did however move for his England colleague Anthony Gordon, paying Newcastle £75m for his services.

‌



On his new winger, Flick added: “At the end, Anthony Gordon comes and from the first call with him, when I first spoke with him, he is on fire with Barca and wants to go there and I am delighted he is on our team.”

Flick’s comments about Rashford come just days after the forward bid farewell to the club on social media. He wrote: "I'm very grateful to everyone at the club for making my time here such a positive and memorable experience.

View 2 Images Barcelona chose not to sign Marcus Rashford permanently (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I've enjoyed every moment and will take many special memories with me. I wish the club and all its supporters the very best of luck and every success in the season ahead."

In all, Rashford made 49 appearances in all competitions for Barcelona during his time in Spain, scoring 14 goals and providing a further 14 assists. The Red Devils academy graduate also spent six months on loan at Aston Villa before joining Barcelona. He still has two years remaining on his contract with United.

Rashford has yet to link up with the Red Devils’ squad on their pre-season tour, having been granted additional time off following the World Cup.

Sports.title: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso gives Mykhailo Mudryk update as winger handed green light to return
Sports.content:
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso gives Mykhailo Mudryk update as winger handed green light to return

Mykhailo Mudryk is available for selection again after the FA resolved his disciplinary proceedings, and Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has shared his thoughts on the returning winger

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso is ready to welcome Mykhailo Mudryk into his Chelsea team (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso has confirmed that Chelsea want Mykhailo Mudryk as part of their team now that the Ukraine international is available to play again. The Football Association (FA) confirmed on Friday that anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against him had been resolved in agreement with the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA).

‌



Mudryk, 25, is no longer ineligible after being provisionally suspended since December 2024 due to a positive doping test for the prohibited substance meldonium. The winger can now return to competition with immediate effect.

‌



Mudryk was officially charged by the FA with anti-doping violations in June 2025 before lodging an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport in February 2026.

‌



Chelsea star Mykhailo Mudryk shares emotional message after doping ban lifted READ MORE :

Mykhailo Mudryk ban LIFTED as FA release statement confirming Chelsea star can play again READ MORE :

In May of this year, the independent body confirmed that 'written submissions' had been exchanged and that a hearing had been scheduled. The four-year ban has now been overturned, and Mudryk, who has not featured in a competitive fixture for the Blues since November 2024, is once again available for selection.

Speaking to journalists at the Accor Stadium in Sydney, Australia, Alonso shed further light on the matter. The Chelsea manager said: "We are happy for him, especially for him.

"Probably, we are not able to understand what we've been through in these moments. We want him to be a part of the team. He has the support of everyone."

‌



View 2 Images Winger Mykhailo Mudryk is now free to play for Chelsea again (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

Alonso continued: "It will take time, but once things have changed, things will start moving. He wants to play football and be part of the team; it must have been really hard for him.

"I watched him at Shakhtar (Donetsk), the impact he had, how good he is in one-v-one situations. He can create a lot of situations on his own.

‌



He's a special player. But it will take time, for sure."

The Blues boss added: "It's massive. To go through what he has done, to go through what he has gone through, it must have been really hard."

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



It is understood that a crucial element in the decision to overturn the ban was WADA's alteration of scientific reporting standards. In an official statement, the FA confirmed that had Mudryk's sample been examined under the current technical standards, he would not have received a suspension, nor would any anti-doping rule violations have been registered.

Throughout the process, which lasted almost two years, Mudryk consistently maintained that he was unaware of taking a prohibited substance. Sources at Stamford Bridge indicate they have backed the Ukrainian, who joined from Shakhtar Donetsk for an initial £62million, plus a further £27m in bonuses, in January 2023.

It is understood that the player is now expected to travel to Hong Kong to link up with the Chelsea squad before Wednesday's pre-season friendly against Juventus.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr to Arsenal latest as Gunners in 'strong position' to seal blockbuster transfer
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr to Arsenal latest as Gunners in 'strong position' to seal blockbuster transfer

Arsenal are keen on a sensational swoop for Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr should he not sign a new contract with the Spanish giants and it appears that a move could actually happen

View 2 Images Arsenal would be willing to offer Vinicius Jr a mega-money contract (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal remain optimistic over a stunning deal for Vinicius Jr should the winger choose not to renew his contract with Real Madrid. The Gunners have explored a deal for the Brazilian wideman this summer, with Mikel Arteta keen on adding to his frontline after ending the club’s long wait for the Premier League crown.

‌



Arsenal have approved a move for Vinicius at all levels of the club but a move now depends on what happens during talks over a new deal. Real are keen to tie the Brazilian down to a new contract - Vinicius’ current deal set to expire in 2027.

‌



But there is an impasse in talks. Vinicius currently banks €18m per season in Spain and has received a renewal offer of around €20m, which was rejected by the winger’s camp.

‌



They have asked for a total package of just under €30m per season which encompasses a base salary, performance-related bonuses and a renewal bonus., albeit are prepared to lower their demands to come to an agreement. As per The Athletic, Real are hesitant to pay a renewal bonus as they are aware that it would set a dangerous precedent within the squad, while they do not want to break their already-established wage cap any further.

New Newcastle boss makes Bruno Guimaraes stance clear amid Arsenal offer READ MORE :

Arsenal star refused to go on pre-season tour to force through summer transfer READ MORE :

From Arsenal’s point of view, they are willing to offer Vinicius a contract that would go beyond their usual wage structure, with the hope that a signing-on bonus and image rights could help them from a financial standpoint.

When it comes to a transfer fee, Arsenal are hopeful that they could seal a deal for a reduced fee given that Real Madrid could lose Vinicius for nothing in 12 months’ time when his contract expires. That is a situation that the Spanish giants are desperate to avoid.

‌



There are also reportedly figures at the Bernabeu in favour of cashing in this summer as opposed to letting him leave as a free agent. But the final decision will ultimately lie with president Florentino Perez.

As it stands, the situation very much hinges on talks over a new deal, with three options being realistic. Either Vinicius pens a new deal with Real Madrid and any talk of an exit is taken off of the table, or he will leave this summer or next for nothing.

View 2 Images Vinicus Jr is out of contract next summer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



When it comes to Mikel Arteta, the Spaniard has underlined his desire to add to his squad ahead of the new campaign. He said: “A lot is happening.

“We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

It's claimed that a fee exceeding £100m would not put Liverpool off. Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz joined at Anfield in transfers worth more than that amount last summer.

Andoni Iraola has previously made it clear that Liverpool are in the market for another winger.. "No, I think it is difficult to say a number when the market is open," Iraola said.

‌



"You have to be always open to new options to improve the squad. There are obvious situations where we need to sign players.

"A winger for example, we definitely need to sign a winger, but there are other situations where we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what is the cost, how we also see the players we have."
