Sports.title: Feisty Battle of Sydney Harbour Bridge between Chelsea and Tottenham saw old rivalries reignited while youngster who suffered brutal humiliation under Igor Tudor is ready to play key role for Roberto De Zerbi, writes KIERAN GILL
Sports.content:
Feisty Battle of Sydney Harbour Bridge between Chelsea and Tottenham saw old rivalries reignited while youngster who suffered brutal humiliation under Igor Tudor is ready to play key role for Roberto De Zerbi, writes KIERAN GILL

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

No such thing as a ‘friendly’ fixture between Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur. Not even when you pick it up and move it to the other side of the planet. For a while here, the locals thought they were being treated to their own Battle of the Sydney Harbour Bridge.

Spurs in particular initially looked like they were more interested in roughing up their fellow tourists. We had Jan Paul van Hecke clattering Joao Pedro, which was an intriguing clash in itself because when they were at Brighton together, the pair were involved in a training-ground punch-up.

Levi Colwill and Dominic Solanke scuffled away from the ball. Conor Gallagher went through Dario Essugo, which led to several Chelsea players surrounding their old pal in anger. Wesley Fofana complained that Gallagher poked him in the eye. Van Hecke elbowed Joao Pedro in the rib cage.

It was feisty, but in a weird way, it was beneficial. It meant this friendly was not played at some snoozy pace, as if the players figured it was simply a practice match. There was an intensity to it all. First, Spurs took the lead via Sandro Tonali’s 20-yard strike which had the help of a Colwill deflection. Then, Chelsea equalised with Jamie Gittens crossing for the head of Estevao Willian.

Spurs seemed in control until Kevin Danso received his red card. The only surprise is that it was not for a nasty challenge, but for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity. Danso had only been on the field for three minutes when he let the ball run behind him and he dragged down Joao Pedro. It was a deserved red, if a little strange to see one actually shown in a friendly.

From then on, Chelsea at least got to practice trying to unlock a deep defensive line. They did not, and Richarlison snatched victory for Spurs in stoppage time by tapping in the rebound.

There was no shortage of feistiness as Chelsea met Tottenham in Sydney Harbour on Saturday

The pre-season tussle was far from friendly at times as both teams sought the bragging rights

Kinsky's comeback

Chelsea really should have won this friendly, and the primary reason they did not was Antonin Kinsky, the goalkeeper who appears to be Roberto De Zerbi’s No 1 choice going into the next season.

Kinsky, 23, should not only be remembered for being substituted after 17 minutes away at Atletico Madrid. He can forge a fine career, perhaps even in the Premier League, if supported properly.

De Zerbi is ready to do that, and it is hard to decide which one of his saves was the best here.

He denied Estevao Willian twice as well as Joao Pedro. When Andy Robertson tried to chest the ball back to Kinsky, it actually fell to Joao Pedro, who was ready to run away in celebration. But Kinsky was there – again.

It was intriguing watching how Spurs set themselves up. When their two central defenders split apart, Kinsky became the third centre back in between them, owing to his passing ability.

Goalkeeper Pending Alonso approval

A minor injury for Robert Sanchez meant Chelsea had to rely on Teddy Sharman-Lowe, 23, in goal. The plan for next season is for Sanchez and Mike Penders to compete together.

Penders is still on his post-World Cup break, but you do wonder whether he should have cut short his downtime to come to Sydney to try to impress Xabi Alonso. Sanchez's small issue could have been an opportunity. Instead, Penders isn't here yet, and Sharman-Lowe started in goal instead.

Teddy Sharman-Lowe will likely be Xabi Alonso's third-choice goalkeeper but he started Down Under with Mike Penders still absent

Penders’ last appearance at club level was for Strasbourg, on loan from Chelsea, on May 17. He went away with Belgium for the World Cup, though went unused in all six of their games, with Thibaut Courtois preferred. The Belgians exited at the quarter-final stage on July 10.

Gittens must continue to impress

During this pre-season, Jamie Gittens has impressed, both in the games played and in training. The Mykhailo Mudryk news is now public. He is set to join up with Chelsea in this pre-season because he can finally return to being a footballer again.

That means Gittens is set for even more competition, from Mudryk and, of course, Morgan Rogers after he joined from Aston Villa for £117million.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi urges Richarlison to make a decision on his Tottenham future as Spurs boss insists he wants Brazilian to STAY: 'All of us love him'
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi urges Richarlison to make a decision on his Tottenham future as Spurs boss insists he wants Brazilian to STAY: 'All of us love him'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted he does not know whether Richarlison wants to stay or leave Tottenham Hotspur and he would like clarity from his striker.

The Brazilian, 29, scored a stoppage-time winner to secure a 2-1 friendly win over Chelsea. Leading the line at the Accor Stadium in Sydney, Richarlison pounced on the rebound after Spurs had struck the post through their youth product Jamie Donley.

Speaking about Richarlison afterwards, De Zerbi said: ‘I don't know. I like him as a player, as a guy, it's unbelievable the attitude and behaviour, but at the end we have to respect what he wants to do.

‘And we know. Every one of us knows what he wants to do, but for me he's still an important player, because it's not so easy to find another striker like Richarlison.

‘Because Richarlison scores goals and he knows the way. The new striker, we don't know. The other striker, we don't know. He scored 12 goals last season, not through luck, because he feels the way to score.’

When pressed on whether he was admitting to us that Richarlison wants to leave Spurs, De Zerbi said: ‘I don't know, I didn't understand well, because sometimes he said to stay, sometimes he leaves. We have to speak anyway. There is not any problem.

Richarlison is a fan favourite at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium but could move on this summer

‘He’s a lovely guy. All of us love him, the team-mates, the club, the staff, because he works hard every day, seriously every day, and we can't say anything on the pitch.’

Meanwhile, amid reports abroad that Spurs have agreed a deal to sell their captain Cristian Romero to Inter Milan, De Zerbi said: ‘I texted with Cuti yesterday to make a plan for when he comes back to London. Not for the transfer market. That's not my job. I know there are many solutions in the transfer market.’

Tottenham are now set to return home to London to continue their pre-season preparations for the Premier League. Their beaten opponents in Chelsea, however, are moving on to Hong Kong, Indonesia and Malaysia.

Sports.title: Humiliated FIFA president Gianni Infantino admits defeat in controversial plot to sell the World Cup in embarrassing U-turn - now he is in a fight to save his job
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has been humiliated after his plan to sell stakes in the World Cup died thanks to the heroics of UEFA, CONCACAF, the AFC and two members of the FIFA hierarchy.

While it appears the FIFA president will fight on to save his job, the Swiss football administrator has abandoned his proposal to sell £3.1billion ($4.1bn) in shares in FIFA tournaments to private investors.

Infantino said: 'The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

'And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

Join the discussion Should football's biggest tournaments ever be open to private investment and ownership?

Gianni Infantino waves goodbye to his unilateral plans for private investment in FIFA

Infantino had hoped to create a new enterprise with significant investment from Joshua Kushner (pictured) - brother of Jared, Donald Trump's son-in-law

Carlos Cordeiro, senior adviser to Infantino and member of the White House World Cup task force 'As a Senior Advisor to the FIFA President, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup. 'Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for FIFA's Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game. 'Selling a permanent stake in football's most valuable asset to raise $4.2 billion makes little sense. It is mortgaging football's future without any compelling justification. 'Most troubling of all is the absence of answers to fundamental questions. Why this deal? Why now? What oversight exists? Who benefits? Was there a competitive process? What governance will be in place? What will investors ultimately gain, and at what cost to football? 'It has been the privilege of a lifetime to serve FIFA for more than five years and to work alongside dedicated, principled people who care deeply about the game. I hope they, too, will speak up, because decisions of this magnitude should be made in the interests of football, not those who stand to profit from it.'

'Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

'Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

'Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, and particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.'

The statement marks an embarrassing u-turn for Infantino, less than 24 hours after he attempted to clarify his plans - blaming the media for misconstruing them.

On Friday, the AFC became the third confederation to reject Gianni Infantino's proposal to raise private capital for the commercial and operational management of FIFA tournaments.

The decision followed CONCACAF's rejection on Thursday and came after UEFA announced a boycott of FIFA competitions. New Zealand Football also objected to the plans, despite the OFC delaying a continent-wide response.

One international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: 'UEFA's response is at the nuclear button end of the spectrum, which is impressive. We thought Infantino would survive the Trump refereeing intervention - but he has overreached this time.'

According to Sky News, UEFA are also thought to have asked for binding assurances that 'FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership' to end their boycott.

It became clear on Friday afternoon that Infantino did not have the support to proceed with his plans, with the opposing nations rising to a staggering 135 - 64 per cent of the FIFA membership.

The proposal appeared to reach a terminal stage when Carlos Cordeiro, senior advisor to Gianni Infantino, announced his resignation from FIFA - becoming the first internal dissident.

Six hours later, FIFA's chief operating officer Kevin Lamour turned against the president - risking his job by criticising the plans and calling on nations to dethrone Infantino. Lamour admitted FIFA Forward Enterprise was the brainchild of 'one person' as he landed a critical blow to the FIFA president.

Carlos Cordeiro (left) quit as an advisor to Gianni Infantino (centre) on Friday

Kevin Lamour, FIFA's Chief Operating Officer 'What has been announced in recent days and what has been happening behind the scenes in recent months defies belief and imagination. 'To put it very clearly and directly: the project that has sparked so much controversy and debate is not a FIFA project. It is even less a project of FIFA's administration. It is the project of one person. FIFA's own administration was deceived. 'Not only must this project not go ahead but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions. Everyone must take responsibility. Because it is becoming increasingly difficult for FIFA's administration to work under these conditions. 'Our mission is to serve football. Not to serve the personal interests of a person who, unfortunately, believes he embodies FIFA when he is supposed to be at its service. A president must bring people together, unite them, and inspire them. Today, we are experiencing the opposite. 'I have no authority to speak on behalf of my colleagues, and perhaps I am mistaken. But my feeling is that we all want to be proud to work for FIFA, and today, unfortunately, it seems that is no longer the case for many of us. That saddens me. The ball is now in the court of those who have the power to change things. 'I know I have a duty of loyalty to my employer. But I also, and above all, have a duty of loyalty to certain values and to the upbringing I have received, and a duty to support my colleagues. And if that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I'll sleep well tonight.'

Infantino had hoped to create a new enterprise with significant investment from Joshua Kushner - brother of Jared, Donald Trump's son-in-law. Meanwhile, investment bank J.P. Morgan were advising on potential investors.

Democratic senator Ron Wyden, who leads an investigation into Jared Kushner, said on Friday: 'Soccer fans around the world are rightfully outraged by this scheme from Infantino and Joshua Kushner to turn the World Cup into just another commodity for private equity to buy up.

'It seems clear from the global backlash that this corrupt plan is unlikely to succeed, but it is just one of dozens of shady deals by Trump's family and close associates to get rich from the presidency.'

A significant number of FIFA members raised concerns from the initial leak of the plan, questioning how such thorough ideas could be developed unilaterally without prior consultation.

Despite FIFA maintaining throughout that there would be a proper consultation period, there were major questions about how that could be achieved when potential investors were already lined up.

UEFA accused FIFA of trying to bribe members with a £30million ($40m) incentive to approve Infantino's plan, with a September 19 deadline to respond to the offer.

Those plans, though, are now dead in the water after Infantino scrapped them at half past midnight (UK) on Saturday.

There is growing opposition to Infantino's presidency, with sources telling Daily Mail Sport that CONCACAF nations believe he is losing or has already lost their confidence.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham believes Infantino's position is untenable and he is not alone.

Speaking to reporters in Sheffield on Friday, Burnham said: 'This was an outrageous suggestion. The idea that it could even be brought forward shows that, in my view, [he] is the wrong man to lead the organisation.'

With the controversy surrounding Infantino, member nations could still trigger a vote of no confidence. The threshold to initiate the process is 46 FIFA member associations.

UEFA and their member associations are yet to be drawn on that matter. Infantino is seeking a fourth term in next year's elections.

Sepp Blatter, Infantino's predecessor, took to social media to renew his attacks on his successor by writing on Friday evening: 'FIFA is not a private equity fund. It is an association with statutes, regulations, and a fiduciary responsibility to protect the global game.

'If you sell football's crown jewels to private investors, you also sell part of the game – especially its soul. Money matters, but it must never become everything.'

Sports.title: Delighted Xabi Alonso hails the return of 'special' Mykhailo Mudryk after Chelsea's £88m star saw his four-year doping ban overturned
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso does not know what will happen next with Mykhailo Mudryk at Chelsea, but says he is looking forward to meeting the unsuspended Ukrainian in Hong Kong and working with him.

Chelsea’s new manager spoke for the first time since it was announced that Mudryk’s four-year doping ban had been cut short. The 25-year-old has not appeared for his club since November 2024 but will now be travelling to Hong Kong to join his team-mates on their pre-season tour.

Chelsea signed Mudryk for £89million from Shakhtar Donetsk in 2023 as he signed an eight-and-a-half-year contract until 2031. His career was then curtailed when he was charged with failing a doping test.

Following developments in the scientific guidance, WADA increased the reporting threshold to provide greater confidence that samples reported as positive exceed the minimum reporting level. The precise source of the exposure has never been entirely identified, but it is believed it occurred while Mudryk was on international duty with Ukraine in September 2024.

‘To be honest, we were not expecting to have this great news at this moment, so we are very happy,’ Alonso said after losing a pre-season friendly, 2-1 to Tottenham, in Sydney, Australia. ‘We feel that he will be working with us.

A delighted Xabi Alonso shared his excitement at working with the unbanned Mykhailo Mudryk

The Ukrainian saw his four-year doping ban overturned on Friday afternoon

‘I remember watching him in Shakhtar (Donetsk), the impact he had, how quick he is, how good in one-on-one situations, how he could create a lot of situations on his own, and he's a special player, but he will take time for sure.

‘We are happy for him, especially for him, because probably we are not able to understand what he has been through in this time. We want that he feels part of a team, because he has been training on his own for a long time, and that we have the support from everyone, from the club, from the team-mates, from the staff, and for sure, it will take time. Once he is with us, we will see how things develop. He is coming to Hong Kong, but I haven't spoken to him yet.’

Asked if Mudryk will be staying with Chelsea or leaving this summer, such as by being sent on loan to their sister side Strasbourg, Alonso said: ‘We need to see. It’s too early to tell, to see how he is in terms of fitness, in terms of this game time that you need to be involved again, so it's still too early to tell. It will take time. For him it's a massive change.

‘He trained on his own every day, and it had to be really, really hard, because he wanted to play football, he wanted to be part of a team, and he was not allowed to do that for such a long time. So once this big change has happened, now things will move on, and afterwards we will see if it's quicker, if it's slower, but we need to be aware of that.’

Sports.title: Revealed: Amateur cricket cheat 'Clicky Ponting' used his notorious finger clicking hoax to get THREE batsmen out in title decider
Sports.content:
Do YOU have a story? Email tips@dailymail.com

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The amateur cricketer whose finger-clicking wicket deception has sparked a global cheating storm apparently once used the same trick to win his team a trophy in a title decider match, the Daily Mail can reveal.

Brian Devine – now known as 'Clicky Ponting' – seems to have hoodwinked umpires to get three opponent batsmen out in a key match in which his side needed a convincing victory to clinch a local league championship.

The proudest moment in Devine's amateur sporting career came when he led former club Pudsey St Lawrence to the Bradford Premier League second tier title in 2023.

The team, which is nicknamed the Saints, had to convincingly beat their oldest rivals Pudsey Congs in a 50-over derby match on the final day of the season if they were to win the trophy.

Devine, the team's captain, was hoping to go out on a high note as it was to be his last ever game for the club.

A day of high drama at their opponent's Amber Cars Britannia ground in the West Yorkshire market town ended in Pudsey St Lawrence winning the title with an emphatic eight wicket victory.

As skipper, Devine, 38, was seen proudly holding aloft the league championship trophy in photographs posted on the club's social media feeds.

But the newly unearthed footage – which was live-streamed at the time and has since been uncovered by the Daily Mail – casts the result of the title-winning match into doubt.

The amateur cricketer whose finger-clicking wicket deception has sparked a global cheating storm apparently once used the same trick to win his team a trophy in a title decider match (pictured), the Daily Mail can reveal

Brian Devine (pictured), who is now known as 'Clicky Ponting', seems to have hoodwinked umpires to get three opponent batsmen out in a key match in which his side needed a convincing victory to clinch a local league championship

It shows Devine apparently attempting to mislead umpires with his finger clicking antics on a series of occasions – leading to wickets falling at crucial points in the game.

The Daily Mail can reveal that three bemused players from the opposing team were given out in almost identical circumstances – after balls flew past their bats at close proximity before landing in the gloves of the wicketkeeper.

Devine is clearly seen clicking his fingers in what appear to be carefully timed routines that mimicked the sound of a ball hitting the bat.

The Daily Mail had already revealed earlier this week how Devine's clicky antics had been dated back a full five years to his days playing for Pudsey St Lawrence.

Now today's fresh revelations have led to calls for the club, which was founded in 1845, to be stripped of the title it won thanks to Devine in 2023.

Members of rival teams – who believe umpires have been routinely misled over a number of years – want the Bradford Premier League to mount a formal investigation.

One source told the Daily Mail: 'Our lads have been looking back at surviving film and score books and we have come to the conclusion that he's been at it for years.

'Young players will have lost opportunities because of this, match results will have undoubtedly been affected, and there is a good case for now stripping Pudsey St Lawrence of its 2023 title.'

The source added: 'Devine was a highly competitive and quite bumptious captain, and the bigger question is of course what club staff and his team-mates did or didn't know about his antics.'

The new revelations come just days after Devine was suspended for the 'foreseeable future' by his current club Saltburn CC over accusations he had used his clicking technique to trick umpires into wrongly giving batsmen out.

The club were placed under investigation by the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League following a complaint made in the aftermath of Saltburn's 159-run win over Norton in a Second XI Division Two match.

Video footage of the incident went viral online and has been reported around the globe – where commentators from England's biggest cricketing rivals including Australia have been leading the condemnation.

Devine – who is company secretary and financial manager of a livestock auction house – is yet to comment on the allegations.

The 2023 title-win proved third time lucky for Pudsey St Lawrence under Devine's captaincy after they had finished third in the table in 2021 and fourth in 2022.

One of the most venerable teams in club cricket, Pudsey St Lawrence has produced two of Yorkshire and England's greatest ever players – Herbert Sutcliffe, who averaged more than 60 in Test matches, and Sir Leonard Hutton, who scored 368 against Australia in 1938.

The new revelations come just days after Devine was suspended for the 'foreseeable future' by his current club Saltburn CC over accusations he had used his clicking technique in a Second XI Division Two match (pictured) against Norton Cricket Club last weekend

A complaint was made in the aftermath of Saltburn's 159-run win last Saturday. Video footage of the incident (pictured) later went viral online and has been reported around the globe

New Zealand stars Mark Greatbatch and Martin Crowe also spent time playing there.

The club has had a longstanding local rivalry with Pudsey Congs where former England pace bowler Matthew Hoggard started out.

There was great anticipation when the teams came face to face on the final day of the season in September 2023.

The Saints – who put out a team made up of a handful of senior cricketers playing alongside young 'homegrown talent' – went into the match knowing they needed a convincing win as two other teams in the league including the then-reigning champions could have overhauled them.

In the footage uncovered by the Daily Mail in which the entire match is shown, spectators sitting on deck chairs positioned behind the boundary can be seen watching on as the drama unfolded on a day of glorious sunshine.

After winning the toss, the home team elected to open the batting and there were 15 runs on the scoreboard when the first wicket fell in the ninth over of the match.

Devine, who was fielding at third slip, can be seen apparently preparing his clicking action as the bowler delivered the first three balls of his over without conceding any runs.

When the batsman takes a hefty swing at the fourth delivery, Devine flamboyantly clicked his fingers as the ball raced past into the wicketkeeper's gloves.

The captain enthusiastically appealed to the umpire along with his other teammates – and the batsman was given out having scored just seven runs.

The bemused-looking player momentarily remains at his crease before walking off towards the pavilion.

Just 16 minutes later, with the score at 31-1, a second player was dismissed in an almost identical way.

The batsman, who had scored one run, apparently nicked the ball while playing a forward defensive shot.

In the background, Devine can be seen carrying out his seemingly well-prepared manoeuvre before leading the appeals for a dismissal.

Again, the umpire raised his finger and the batsman trudged off with the score at 31-2.

It was not until the 36th over of the match that Devine was apparently able to utilise his unique talent again.

With the score at 117-5, he moved himself into the position of first slip.

Two balls later, with the wicketkeeper standing up to the wicket, Devine apparently clicked his fingers again as the ball went past the bat into the keeper's gloves.

The batsman, who had scored just one run, stepped back into his crease as Devine led noisy celebrations.

When the match official confirmed that the batsman had been caught out, the player momentarily stood his ground as he appeared to question the decision.

He is seen repeatedly shaking his head as he walked off the pitch – once again in apparent disbelief.

In the end, Pudsey Congs slumped to a disappointing 142 all out after just 42.5 overs of play.

Devine went on to open the batting for his team – facing the very first ball of the innings.

He was the second batsman to lose his wicket, scoring just four runs before he was caught out after clearly edging the ball into the hands of the wicketkeeper – leaving his team struggling at 25-2.

Despite the early setback, his team quickly turned things around and took a firm grip of the match.

They suffered no further loss of wickets as they raced to a winning total with 76 balls remaining.

The title-winning team were applauded enthusiastically by delighted supporters who rose to their feet after the winning runs were scored.

Further footage of a Bradford Premier League match in August 2021 has also come to light, leading to claims Devine began his cheating antics as long as five years ago.

Only a tiny number of matches were filmed at the time but statistics show that during the three seasons Devine captained Pudsey St Lawrence, this particular wicketkeeper took 96 catches – an average of 32 per year.

After his championship-winning exploits, Devine returned to Saltburn, his childhood club, the following season.

In the two years that followed his departure, the wicketkeeper in question took 22 and 15 catches respectively. So far this season, he's managed just five.

The Daily Mail revealed earlier this week how Devine's clicky antics had been dated back a full five years to his days playing for Pudsey St Lawrence. Pictured: Footage from a Bradford Premier League match in August 2021, in which he can be seen repeatedly clicking his fingers

Club officials, however, insist they had never received a complaint from opponents over the cricketer's behaviour.

Martin Reed, Chairman at Pudsey St Lawrence Cricket Club, told the Daily Mail: 'We were not aware of any issues with Mr Devine's behaviour during his time at the club, nor were concerns raised with us by other clubs or officials.

'Had we been made aware of any issues at the time we would have taken appropriate action.

'It is some time since Mr Devine left Pudsey St Lawrence and we are aware that the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League and Saltburn Cricket Club are currently investigating the matter.'

Sports.title: Top jockey Jim Crowley retires at 48 after horror fall at York led to five operations
Sports.content:
Top jockey Jim Crowley retires at 48 after horror fall at York led to five operations

The retained rider to top owner/breeders Shadwell announced his decision at the end of the Qatar Goodwood Festival, where he rode the sprinter Battaash to win a record four runnings of the King George Stakes

View 2 Images Jim Crowley (Image: Getty Images)

Top jockey Jim Crowley has retired at the age of 48 and revealed a plan to turn his hand to training racehorses later this year.

‌



The champion of the 2016 season said he had thought long and hard about whether he could return to racing, after his recovery from serious injuries sustained when Almeraq fell in a race at York in September 2025.

‌



However Crowley felt he could not reach the level of fitness required to continue his stellar career, in which he was associated with numerous top horses wearing the silks of late owner Sheikh Hamdan Al Maktoum.

‌



"I've had five operations, the last of them three weeks ago," he told the Racing Post. "Mentally, I still think I can do it, but physically, it's just not possible to get back to the level I would want to reach."

Crowley's announcement comes on the final day of the Qatar Goodwood Festival, a track where he partnered brilliant sprinter Battaash to a record four wins in the Group Two King George Stakes over five furlongs.

He also enjoyed a fine time with Baaeed, celebrating Group One successes in the 2021 Prix Du Mouin at Longchamp, Queen Elizabeth II Stakes at Ascot and the following year's Lockinge, Queen Anne Stakes, Sussex Stakes and Juddmonte International.

‌



Crowley, who started a decade over jumps in 1997 and switched to the Flat full-time in 2006, also linked up with Shadwell stars like Hukum, Mostahdaf and Anmaat.

But he was forced to put his career on hold when he sustained pelvic and leg fractures in the fall on the Knavesmire last year. He was riding Almeraq for Shadwell and trainer William Haggas when the colt appeared to clip the heels of a horse in front, in the process bringing down another runner, ridden by Trevor Whelan, who was also hurt.

View 2 Images Battaash and Jim Crowley at Goodwood (Image: PA)

‌



"The injuries I suffered have made me realise how fortunate I've been to enjoy such a long career doing something I absolutely loved," Crowley added.

"Holding the Shadwell job for so long was amazing. They are such loyal people. It has been a pleasure to ride for Sheikha Hissa, her father and the family, and I've also enjoyed working with Angus Gold and Richard Hills."

In June, Crowley ruled himself out of Royal Ascot, telling Mirror Racing: “I’ve been riding out and I’m just not up to race riding yet. Ascot has come a little too soon. Although I could probably turn up it’s not where I want it to be and I want it to be 100 percent. You can’t come into a meeting like this at the top stage if you are not 100 percent.

Article continues below

“It’s hard but one thing I have learnt is racing is a great leveller and it is at the end of the day horses running around a field. It’s not the end of the world. There are lot more worse off than me.”

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham shows true colours as England hero sent on Barcelona 'spying mission'
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham shows true colours as England hero sent on Barcelona 'spying mission'

Jude Bellingham appeared at a Barcelona pre-season game

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham watched his former club Birmingham take on Barcelona (Image: Getty Images)

Jude Bellingham changed his outfit midway through his former club Birmingham City's pre-season friendly clash with Barcelona. The Real Madrid sensation took the opportunity to observe his bitter rivals Barca ahead of the new season, where the two Spanish giants are expected to go toe-to-toe for the La Liga crown once more.

‌



Bellingham returned to his boyhood club Birmingham on Friday in his first public appearance since returning to the UK from his holiday in Hawaii. The trip came after his heroics for England at the World Cup, where his seven goals launched him into an entirely new stratosphere.

‌



The Three Lions superstar was spotted in attendance at St. Andrew’s alongside his parents Denise and Mark. His appearance in the stands didn’t go unnoticed as he was cheered and given a rousing ovation by the home crowd.

‌

Jude Bellingham's parting shot to Argentina referee in unseen World Cup footage READ MORE :

Bellingham was seen celebrating both of Birmingham's goals in the entertaining 2-2 draw and he even stayed for the penalty shootout, which Chris Davies’ side won.

Upon his arrival, the 23-year-old wore a plain white top before slipping into the new Birmingham jersey at half-time. His touching gesture clearly endeared himself further to the Blues fans.

‌



Bellingham made his senior debut for Birmingham as a 16-year-old and quickly established himself as one of the brightest young talents in English football. His rapid development earned him a move to Borussia Dortmund, where he became one of Europe's top midfielders before joining Real Madrid in the summer of 2023.

View 2 Images He changed into a Birmingham shirt in a heart-warming moment at St Andrew's (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

His move helped the Blues at a time of financial difficulty, and they retired the No.22 shirt for his services to the club, despite him being a mere teenager at the time. His appearance on Friday wouldn't have only pleased Birmingham supporters, however.

‌



His new Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho would have also been delighted to see him observing rivals Barcelona, given he can now report back to the Portuguese head coach with a fresh report on the Catalans.

Barca were missing the bulk of their squad on Friday due to the World Cup, with coach Hansi Flick forced to name an inexperienced side after a week of training at St. George's Park.

The Catalans were without all eight of their Spain internationals who lifted the trophy in North America this summer. Anthony Gordon, Jules Kounde and Raphinha did not feature, either, although there was a debut for summer signing Karim Adeyemi.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino is so delusional he does not know his time is well and truly up
Sports.content:
Of the many remarkable things about the whole World Cup sell-off saga, one stands out. Power had made Gianni Infantino so delusional he thought his plot would not be destroyed by all those who care about football. Power had detached him from reality. Infantino is an intelligent man. A multi-linguist, a highly-qualified lawyer.

So how did he ever think his proposal to allow private investors to run the World Cup would even get a semblance of support from ANYONE with a remote interest in the game? How can you not read the room? How can you be so detached from reality?

Because power has made you feel untouchable. It beggars belief but it really does seem as though the proposal which has now been ditched was entirely the work of Infantino himself, aided, you assume, by his investor acquaintances who were looking to make hundreds of millions out of the World Cup.

Because anyone else in the world’s governing body could have seen what was coming. Outrage on a scale football governance has not known before.

‌



But even his chief operating officer (COO) did not know. Of all the statements denouncing Infantino and his plan, Kevin Lamour’s was the most damning.

He called it ‘the project of one person’. Lamour, FIFA COO spoke about ‘a lack of trust, a lack of transparency, a lack of discernment, a lack of good governance, and a serious lack of respect.’ He spoke of 'contempt' and 'intimidation'.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino was clearly delighted to be considered a friend of Donald Trump's (Image: Getty Images)

Lamour said ‘FIFA’s own administration was deceived’. And of the many reasons why Infantino’s position is untenable, they do not come any more emphatic than that.

‌



“Our mission,” says Lamour, “is to serve football. Not to serve the personal interests of a person who, unfortunately, believes he embodies FIFA when he is supposed to be at its service.”

And there you have it. Power has made Infantino delusional. In the late-night statement announcing the abrupt termination of his heinous scheme, there was no contrition from Infantino.

Instead, he said the scheme “was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.” If that was the case, how come he did not, by the looks of it, consult ANYONE in the FIFA organisation when hatching the plan?

View 3 Images UEFA and its president Aleksander Ceferin dealt the killer blow to Gianni Infantino's World Cup scheme (Image: Getty Images)

‌



In his statement shelving the proposals, he also talks about ‘moving forward’, but quite clearly, FIFA cannot move forward when its president has lost the confidence of the overwhelming majority of stakeholders in the game. And when we say ‘overwhelming majority’, we could probably say ‘all’.

The next president will be elected in March at a congress in Morocco. As it stands, Infantino will be unopposed.

That cannot happen. Other candidates need to come forward ahead of a nomination deadline in November. But the election should happen sooner because Infantino should resign.

All those nations who got together to oppose Infantino’s FIFA Forward Enterprise project should now declare their complete lack of confidence in the organisation’s leader. His time is well and truly up. But the power has made him so delusional, he probably does not know it.

‌

Sports.title: UEFA declare loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino in bombshell new statement
Sports.content:
UEFA declare loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino in bombshell new statement

Gianni Infantino has scrapped his controversial plan to sell off a share of the World Cup to private investors but his move has left European football furious

View 2 Images UEFA have hit back at Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

UEFA have declared a loss of confidence in beleaguered FIFA president Gianni Infantino after his World Cup sale scandal.

‌



Infantino confirmed the plot to sell-off a share in the tournament to private investors this week, only to perform a dramatic u-turn after considerable backlash.

‌



UEFA threatened a wide-ranging boycott of any FIFA tournaments, while fellow federations such as CONCACAF and AFC also publicised their opposition to the plan. O ne of Infantino’s closest advisors, Carlos Cordeiro, resigned from his post, while FIFA Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour slammed the plan.

‌



Things have now grown even worse for the FIFA president, with European football's governing body remaining furious and demanding he be removed from office.

A statement from UEFA read: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

‌



"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA's Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,' before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It's not the money of the FIFA President. It's your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent."

‌



Infantino, 56, has been president of FIFA since February 2016, having replaced Sepp Blatter. He previously worked at UEFA, having been at the corporation since 2000. He claimed the role as Secretary General in 2009 before receiving the backing of the UEFA Executive Committee to stand for the position of FIFA President in 2015.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been forced to perform an embarrassing u-turn (Image: Getty Images)

UEFA's bombshell statement comes less than 12 hours after FIFA confirmed that they had completed a u-turn and scrapped their plan.

‌



A statement in the early hours of Saturday morning read: “The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

“And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

“Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

‌



“Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

“Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino issues new statement as feelings clear after failed World Cup plans
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino issues new statement as feelings clear after failed World Cup plans

Gianni Infantino's grand plans for the World Cup lay in tatters

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been forced into a humiliating climbdown (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Gianni Infantino issued a shameless statement just hours after his plans to sell off the World Cup were embarrassingly ripped to shreds. The controversial FIFA boss had proposed to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) to manage its competitions, including the World Cup.

‌



The most contentious aspect of the plan was the intention to sell a 20 per cent stake to private investors. Thrive Eternal, a company founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, had been earmarked as the lead investor. The plan was met with outcry across the football world, especially in Europe, with all 55 UEFA member associations vowing to boycott the World Cup.

‌



The Asian Confederation and CONCACAF (the association of North America and the Caribbean) also denounced Infantino's scheme. With his plot - and possibly his hold on the FIFA presidency - crumbling around him, Infantino took the time to issue a tin-eared statement highlighting the success and "unity" of the recent World Cup.

‌



On Saturday morning, the Swiss administrator took to Instagram to post: "The FIFA World Cup 2026 brought together more people, more cultures and more communities than ever before, showing the true power of the beautiful game.

"Football speaks every language and belongs to everyone. That is why I have always believed it has a unique ability to bring people together, inspire hope and create opportunities. Thank you to every fan for making this the greatest and most inclusive @fifaworldcup ever."

‌



The post included a picture of him shaking hands with a fan and ended with the hashtag #FootballUnitesTheWorld. The post attracted a few thousand likes but no comments, as they had been disabled.

Following such a stinging response to his plan, including from some of his own colleagues, Infantino has been forced into a humiliating climbdown.

In a separate statement released on Saturday, Infantino said: "The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

‌



View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has taken every opportunity to cosy up to Donald Trump (Image: Photo by Eric Verhoeven/Soccrates/Getty Images)

"And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

"Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

‌



"Our purpose has always been – and will always be – to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

Sports.title: Football fans' power still strong as Gianni Infantino's World Cup plot follows Super League to scrap heap
Sports.content:
Football fans' power still strong as Gianni Infantino's World Cup plot follows Super League to scrap heap

Football fans have long been led to believe that they are losing control of the game they fell in love with but after Gianni Infantino’s dramatic U-turn, they have been shown that they can still make an impact

View 4 Images Gianni Infantino has been forced to perform an embarrassing u-turn on his plans for the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

FIFA’s embarrassing plan to sell the World Cup lasted less than four days before it was scrapped. Under-fire president Gianni Infantino, whose position now appears to be untenable, only unveiled the woeful plot on Thursday.

‌



The reaction was instant. Football didn’t want this. And through the combined power of football supporters, governing federations and even some of Infantino’s closest advisors, the plan has landed on the scrap heap.

‌



In an effort to potentially save face, the FIFA president released a statement in the early hours of Saturday morning confirming that the plan had been cancelled entirely.

‌



It read: “The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

“And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

“Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

‌



“Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

“Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.”

And while Infantino will attempt to hide his humiliating u-turn, football fans should celebrate that their strength has seen the idea binned. They were of course helped by threats of boycotts from UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation - as well as Infantino’s senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro resigning from his position.

‌



View 4 Images Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president is surely untenable (Image: Getty Images)

It left the 56-year-old in a near-impossible position as revealed by UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister. Speaking after the news, she said: "He had to be pushed into that corner and that is regrettable of course, but I think it showed the unity of football when we face such an existential crisis.

"But it really shouldn't have come to this, I think most of us believe this was a hugely misguided and potentially catastrophic proposal and it should never have been put on the table. I am delighted we were able to fight it off."

‌



It is of course not the first time that the sheer power of fans has forced football governance to alter its course - the most infamous example being the plot behind the European Super League back in 2021.

The scandalous project was officially confirmed on April 18, with 20 of Europe’s biggest clubs confirmed to be part of it. The backlash was again instant.

View 4 Images Chelsea supporters protested against the European Super League plot (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Fans mobilised with protests outside of their club’s stadiums, the UK Government expressed its displeasure over the plans and ironically Infantino publicised his opposition. Players also spoke out, while high-profile managers including Arsene Wenger, Jurgen Klopp and Sir Alex Ferguson slammed the plot.

UEFA and FIFA (again, ironically) tried to intervene but the organisers of the Super League hit back with threats of legal proceedings in European courts designed to block any sanctions that they might have in mind.

Under the crippling weight of the fan and governing body backlash, the first cracks in the Super League plot began to show. Just 56 hours after the initial announcement, Manchester City became the first club to pull out and they were eventually followed by all of their Premier League rivals.

‌



And just like that, the European Super League was dead in just a matter of days - allowing for a couple of rogue clubs who were bizarrely willing to pursue the plans for years - but that’s another story.

View 4 Images Man City were the first Premier League side to back out of the Super League plan (Image: Getty Images)

It’s now taken less than a week for Infantino’s baffling plot to be unpicked. Football has come together to decide its future for itself.

‌



In an age where the game seems to be moving away from the common man and closer to the elite - as evidenced by the sky-high prices of this summer's World Cup - it’s heartening to know that there is still the potential for the normal, match-going supporter to have an impact on the future of the beautiful game.

It leaves Infantino in an untenable position. His intentions are now clear. While he has been able to stomach a humiliating defeat, whether he is now able to relinquish his power right at the top of FIFA remains to be seen.

Should football fans want him gone, he needs to make sure that he doesn’t underestimate their opinions. After all, he too could end up lasting days.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's World Cup final behaviour sparks petition to strip him of prestigious award
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's World Cup final behaviour sparks petition to strip him of prestigious award

A prestigious honour recently awarded to Lionel Messi is facing calls to be withdrawn following a furious backlash sparked by the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup final

View 3 Images Lionel Messi could have is award stripped (Image: AFP or licensors)

Calls for Lionel Messi to be stripped of the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports have intensified in the wake of the 2026 World Cup final. The prestigious honour - presented to individuals and organisations for outstanding contributions to sport, science, the humanities and public affairs - was awarded to the Argentine icon in June.

‌



In explaining its decision, the jury pointed not only to Messi's extraordinary achievements on the pitch but also praised his extensive charitable work, his exemplary on-field conduct and his perseverance, humility and commitment to team play.

‌



But that decision has since come under intense scrutiny following Argentina's 1-0 defeat to Spain in last month's World Cup final. Tempers flared at the final whistle as several Argentine players became embroiled in heated confrontations with their Spanish counterparts.

‌



Although Messi did not take part in any of the physical clashes, he and his team-mates drew criticism by turning their backs and refusing to watch Spain's trophy presentation - a gesture widely condemned as lacking in sportsmanship.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lionel Messi's gesture to Argentina squad leaked after World Cup dressing room theories READ MORE :

The backlash has prompted multiple petitions calling for Messi to be stripped of the Princess of Asturias Award, with critics arguing his actions fell short of the standards of conduct the honour is intended to recognise.

‌



One petition argues that Messi displayed behaviour that was "unsportsmanlike and contrary to the values of respect and fair play that the sport promotes." It also states that stripping him of the award would "send a clear message about the importance of maintaining exemplary conduct in all facets of life, especially in the realm of sports."

Another initiative maintains that revoking the honour would help "restore confidence in the fairness and rigour" of these awards, which have been awarded to the likes of Al Gore, David Attenborough, Rafael Nadal and Stephen Hawking.

View 3 Images Messi finished runner-up in the World Cup for the second time in his career (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Messi, 39, is due to receive the award at a ceremony in October. When announcing him as the recipient, the Princess of Asturias Foundation said: "In addition to [Messi's] dazzling talent, the Jury has highlighted his exceptional sporting career and his formidable and continued charitable work to promote access to education and health care for the most disadvantaged children.

"Leo Messi, the player who has won the most titles in the history of football, has also earned the respect and admiration of everyone for his exemplary behaviour on the field and for his consistency, humility and commitment to the team game."

Messi was denied the fairy-tale ending to his international career as Argentina fell to a 1-0 extra-time defeat against Spain in the World Cup final in New Jersey. Ferran Torres struck the decisive goal shortly after Enzo Fernandez had been sent off, bringing Argentina's title defence to a heartbreaking conclusion.

‌



View 3 Images The Argentina players all stood with their backs to Spain as the winners received their World Cup medals (Image: Maja Hitij - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Spain were worthy winners, dominating proceedings from start to finish. They enjoyed 68 per cent possession and fired 20 shots at goal, while Argentina managed just three attempts - all of them coming only after falling behind in extra time.

The match, however, was ultimately overshadowed by chaotic scenes after the final whistle. Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes is among several individuals under investigation by FIFA after being charged with three counts of violent conduct. The midfielder was seen physically manhandling two Spain players during the post-match confrontations.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
